description: Host attribution for room timeline chat events is no longer based only on the resolved host address. The new pickEffectiveHostAddress() helper first checks whether the resolved host address appears in the current chat window, but if it does not, it marks the most active sender in that window as the effective host. For room 1659, the resolved host can be the Hyperliquid portfolio wallet rather than the actual chat sender, so this fallback is expected to trigger. An attacker who can post in the room can send enough messages to become the most active sender and have their messages marked isHost=true. The /positions UI and Hermit position marker commands trust isHost for Host-only filtering and labeling, so attacker-controlled messages can be presented as host messages. This does not directly bypass authentication or move funds, but it compromises the integrity of a social-signal trading surface and can mislead users relying on host-only markers.

title: Telegram alert test leaks linked chat ID in room replies
description: The commit adds an alert test flow that resolves the Telegram chat ID for the caller's wallet and, on successful delivery, includes that raw `chatId` in the command response: `Telegram alert test sent ✅ (chat ${chatId}).` `resolveTelegramChatIdForWallet` reads `telegram_user_id` from the `telegram_user_links` table, so this value is a Telegram-linked identifier. In the AlfaClub chat command path, Hermit command results are copied into `response` and returned for posting back to the chat room. This can disclose a user's Telegram user/chat ID to other room participants when the user runs the test command in a shared room. The response should avoid including the raw chat ID, or only display a masked/non-sensitive confirmation.

title: Sampled Telegram action tokens become unredeemable
description: The changed `createTelegramActionToken` function now calls `shouldSampleEvent('telegram_action_tokens', userId:actionType)` and returns `{ token, expiresAt }` without inserting a row when the sample decision is false. However, `telegram_action_tokens` is not telemetry-only; it is the backing capability table for single-use Telegram callback tokens and stores the hashed token plus the intent payload. `consumeTelegramActionToken` later validates callbacks by updating/selecting `telegram_action_tokens` by `token_hash`. A token skipped by sampling has no database row and therefore can never be consumed. Because the sampling key is deterministic and does not include the random token or timestamp, any user/action pair outside the sample bucket is persistently unable to complete that action while the effective sample rate is below 1.0. This impacts Telegram trade, deploy, status-refresh, and similar confirmation flows. It fails closed rather than enabling unauthorized actions, but it can deny availability of security-sensitive transaction/deployment workflows under the documented sampling configuration.

title: Unauthenticated healthcheck leaks live trading risk
description: The healthcheck server accepts unauthenticated requests to `/`, `/health`, and `/healthz` and binds on `0.0.0.0`. This commit adds `currentPosition` to that response and populates it with the live Hyperliquid mark, liquidation distance, ROE, and `isDangerous` flag. If the Railway service or any deployment exposes this port publicly, an attacker can continuously poll the endpoint to learn the monitored wallet's current risk and liquidation proximity. The commit also sends a startup message to the public Telegram channel with the watched wallet, alert thresholds, and the existence of `/health`, making the operational monitoring setup easier to discover. This does not directly move funds, but it can aid adversarial trading or liquidation pressure against the watched position.

title: Healthcheck leaks risk watcher wallet and liveness
description: The commit changes the risk watcher's healthcheck from a static 'ok' response to a JSON payload containing the monitored wallet address, last successful tick timestamp, last tick status, and process uptime. The server binds to 0.0.0.0 and is started automatically when the platform provides PORT, which is typical for Railway deployments. If the service has a public Railway URL or is otherwise reachable, any unauthenticated requester can identify the monitored trading wallet and determine whether the risk watcher is stale or failing. This does not expose signing keys or directly allow asset movement, but it leaks operational intelligence that can help an attacker time market manipulation, liquidation pressure, or alert-evasion attempts against the watched position.

title: Public /alfa status leaks bridge auth health
description: Before this change, detailed AlfaClub auth health was served by a CRON_SECRET-gated endpoint. The commit wires /alfa status to formatAlfaClubStatusForChat(), which reads the live chat_jwt row metadata and auth health snapshot, then returns JWT expiry timing, writer identity, refresh timestamps, refresh failure code path, and bridge failure/backoff counters. The alfaclub command family is dispatched without a role check or chat-scope check, and Telegram/XMTP deterministic command paths can invoke it. No raw JWT is returned, but the newly exposed metadata is useful operational reconnaissance and bypasses the intended secret-gated health endpoint.

title: AlfaClub /alfa bypasses read and kill-switch flags
description: This commit replaced the default /alfa leaderboard path with buildAlfaClubBriefContext()/formatAlfaClubLeaderboardChat() and added /alfa brief using the same context builder. The existing formatter still contains explicit kill-switch and read-enabled redaction logic, but the new successful paths do not call it. buildAlfaClubBriefContext reads the latest snapshot, prior snapshot, creator list, recent publications, labels, and room links unconditionally. As a result, if an operator disables the AlfaClub vigilante read surface or turns on the kill switch while old snapshot rows remain in the database, any caller who can invoke /alfa or /alfa brief can still retrieve the leaderboard/digest and room-link data. Before this change, the default leaderboard path used loadLeaderboard(flags), which returned no rows when readEnabled was false, and then formatLeaderboard(), which redacted output for both killSwitch and !readEnabled.

title: Post-upgrade hook verification accepts incomplete bytecode
description: The commit broadens the post-upgrade bytecode check from requiring `relay_entries`/`RelayEntries` to accepting `relay_entries`, `RelayEntries`, or `SettleFees`. Because these alternatives are ORed together, a deployed program dump that contains `SettleFees` but does not contain the required `relay_entries` instruction will be reported as `canonical relay_entries / settle_fees bytecode OK`. This is especially relevant when the documented `--skip-build --execute` path is used, because the pre-deploy build script's stricter `relay_entries` check is bypassed. The hook program exposes both `settle_fees` and `relay_entries` as separate keeper-only instructions; accepting evidence of only one instruction can mask a bad upgrade and later break lottery entry relay or allow a malicious/stale artifact to be incorrectly recorded as successfully verified.

title: Charm auth helper allows non-keeper delegate fallthrough
description: resolveCharmAutomationAuthorization checks whether rebalanceDelegate equals the keeper, but if it does not, the function does not reject. When charmKeeper and charmOwner are null, the mere presence of any delegateAddress prevents the charm_automation_not_configured rejection, and the final fallback returns { authorized: true, lane: 'keeper_direct' }. This is unsafe for modern/non-legacy Charm vaults that expose manager/rebalanceDelegate but not keeper/owner, or where those reads fail: a delegate controlled by another address is treated as sufficient authorization for the keeper. executeCharmRebalanceManager trusts this result and submits a direct rebalance from the keeper EOA. On-chain Charm authorization should prevent unauthorized state changes, so this is not a direct fund-theft issue, but it can make the keeper repeatedly attempt unexecutable rebalances, causing automation errors/resource waste and potentially clogging strategy maintenance workflows.

title: Pinata production secret IDs exposed in runbook
description: The added Hermit Pinata rebuild documentation includes the exact `--secret <uuid>` identifiers for the production agent's attached secrets. Although these are not the secret values themselves, they are opaque secret-manager resource identifiers for sensitive items such as OpenAI, AlfaClub, cron, database, Pinata, and Supabase service-role credentials. In a public or broadly shared repository this leaks internal secret inventory and makes any later Pinata account/API compromise or authorization bug easier to exploit, because an attacker no longer needs to discover which secret resources to attach or target. The runbook should use placeholders or a private secret inventory instead of real secret IDs; consider rotating/recreating the exposed Pinata secret objects if the provider treats IDs as sensitive or if access logs show unexpected use.

title: Admin control-plane audit attribution can be spoofed
description: The newly exposed provision and operator-action endpoints authenticate the caller as an admin, but then trust an optional request-body `requestedBy` field when queuing the privileged workflow. Because `requestedBy` is written into control-plane operations and status-transition event actors, an authenticated admin session can forge audit attribution as another user or arbitrary string. The new maintenance endpoint has the opposite problem: it queues the workflow without passing the authenticated admin at all, so the lower layer records the actor as `system`. This does not grant non-admin access, but it weakens accountability and incident response for privileged workflows.

title: Unsafe Twitter media URL fetch enables SSRF and DoS
description: The commit introduces `downloadTweetMedia`, which accepts a caller-provided media URL and fetches it directly from the backend. The only URL validation is a regex requiring the original string to start with `https://`. The fetch uses default redirect handling, so an attacker-controlled HTTPS URL can redirect the server to internal HTTP/HTTPS resources. There is also no DNS/IP validation to block localhost, RFC1918, link-local, or metadata ranges, no AbortController timeout, and no Content-Length or streaming byte limit before `response.arrayBuffer()` loads the entire response into memory. A malicious media URL can therefore be used for SSRF, server-side request smuggling to internal services reachable from the deployment environment, or memory/connection exhaustion. The code also trusts a caller-supplied `contentType` before the response header and only checks MIME strings rather than image magic bytes, making it easier to pass non-image internal responses into the upload path.

title: Chart tweets bypass Telegram preview-only confirmation
description: Telegram command processing is configured to run Twitter commands in `preview_only` mode so typed `--confirm` flags do not immediately post to X; direct posting is supposed to happen only through the callback path using `allow_direct_confirm`. However, the guard that strips confirm flags only recognizes `/x post` and `/tweet`. This commit adds `/x chart ... --confirm`, and `handleTwitterCommand` treats that flag as authorization to build a chart and call `postTweet` immediately. As a result, an ADMIN/OWNER Telegram user can bypass the intended extra inline-button confirmation for this new posting path. The chart preview path also reuses the generic `twitter.preview_post` action with only `tweetText`, so any generated Telegram preview button will later execute `/x post ... --confirm`, losing the chart attachment rather than posting the chart.

title: Hermit swallows fatal exceptions and stays ready
description: The new process-level handlers in frontend/server/agent/hermit/index.ts log uncaughtException and unhandledRejection events but do not shut down, restart, or mark the runtime unready. In Node.js, resuming normal operation after an uncaughtException is unsafe because the process may be in an undefined state. This Hermit service also exposes readiness from state.bridgeStarted, which is set during startup and is not cleared by the new fatal-error handlers. As a result, if attacker-controlled chat/websocket/API input or an unexpected dependency edge case triggers an uncaught exception in an async callback, Railway or another supervisor may continue routing to a broken process instead of restarting it. The safer pattern is to catch expected transient errors at their source, and for uncaughtException either perform minimal cleanup and exit non-zero, or at least mark readiness false and stop accepting work.

title: Public monitoring views bypass RLS privacy
description: The new migration correctly treats `zora_csw_indexer_state` as service-role-only, and the existing `zora_csw_owners` / `zora_csw_owner_class` tables are also intended to be service-role-only. However, the migration then creates three views in the exposed `public` schema over those private tables. On Supabase/Postgres, views are security-definer by default unless created with `security_invoker = true`, and Supabase public-schema objects are commonly exposed to `anon`/`authenticated` via PostgREST unless grants are revoked. As a result, clients may be able to query these views and bypass the RLS protections on the underlying tables. The leaked data is aggregate operational and wallet-classification telemetry rather than raw owner rows, so the impact is limited, but it contradicts the service-role-only access model. Remediation: create the views with `WITH (security_invoker = true)` on Postgres 15+, move them to a non-exposed schema, or explicitly revoke `SELECT` from `anon` and `authenticated` and grant only trusted roles.

title: Auth-failure path suppresses its own WebSocket fallback
description: On a room-history 401/403, `runBridgeTick` now calls `rememberBadJwt(historyErrorJwt, now)` and then attempts to enter the WebSocket live-fallback path with `ingestJwt`. In the default configuration, `ingestJwt` is the same as `commandJwt`, and `historyErrorJwt` is initialized to `commandJwt`. Therefore `ensureLiveCommandSocket` immediately sees the fallback JWT as known-bad, closes an existing matching live socket, records a suppressed attempt, and returns without opening the fallback connection. This defeats the live fallback that is supposed to preserve command processing when room history fails, including 403 cases with Cloudflare/WAF details that may not imply the WebSocket token is invalid. Repeated history auth failures can keep the bridge from receiving live commands until history recovers or a distinct explicit ingest JWT is configured.

title: Dev loopback redirect can become an open redirect
description: The new `resolveDisallowedLoopbackRedirectUrl` is intended to redirect unsupported loopback development ports back to the configured app origin while preserving path, query, and fragment. However, it constructs the target with `new URL(current.pathname + current.search + current.hash, configured.origin)`. In WHATWG URL parsing, a string beginning with `//` is a network-path reference. Therefore, visiting a dev URL such as `http://localhost:58492//evil.example/phish#token` can produce `http://evil.example/phish#token` instead of `http://localhost:5173//evil.example/phish#token`. `main.tsx` then passes that value to `window.location.replace`. This is limited to `import.meta.env.DEV` and loopback origins, so production impact is low, but it is still an introduced open redirect in local development flows and could be abused for phishing or to leak fragment data in dev/OAuth-style callback scenarios.

title: Timelock state getter is unreachable on main and reads wrong storage
description: The new timelock state view is implemented only in `CreatorLotteryManagerAdminModule`, while the main contract (which owns real state) does not expose a delegating read stub. Because the admin module is a separate contract with separate storage, direct `eth_call` to `getBoostSourceTimelockState()` reads the module's local slots, not the live manager slots. Mutating admin functions are guarded by `onlyDelegateCall`, so module-local timelock slots remain unset in normal operation, making this getter effectively report default values. This can undermine the intended 24h detection window if monitoring systems follow the documented approach and poll this getter, creating a blind spot for pending malicious `boostManager`/`vaultGaugeVoting` changes.

title: Enroll endpoint leaks RPC internals on CSW probe failure
description: In `POST /api/arch-b/enroll`, the new parent-account validation path catches bytecode probe errors and includes `err.message` in the HTTP response body (`data.message`). The probe uses a client built from `BASE_RPC_URL`. Viem/provider errors commonly embed request URL/context, so a failing probe can expose infrastructure details to authenticated callers. This is an information disclosure issue introduced by the new error handling path. While conditional on probe failure, it is remotely triggerable against this endpoint and leaks operational metadata that should remain server-side (log only).

title: Deploy config endpoint no longer enforces admin-only access
description: The deploy configuration endpoint previously enforced an admin-only check before returning deployment runtime settings. The current version removes that admin gate and only verifies that a principal address exists. As a result, any authenticated user can obtain internal configuration values such as the active deployment batcher address, payout router keeper address, and approved swap targets/spenders. While these values are not private keys, they disclose privileged operational metadata and allowlists that were previously restricted, which can aid targeted attacks or reconnaissance.

title: Chat bridge fallback can replay historical commands
description: The new websocket fallback path marks the bridge as seeded when room history returns a 401. Because no history IDs are seeded in this path, the next successful history fetch skips the “first tick” guard and processes all unseen historical messages. This can replay commands that were sent before the bridge started or during an auth outage, causing delayed execution of actions (e.g., trades/deploys) once the JWT is restored.

title: Inline edit postMessage enables cross-origin screenshot exfiltration
description: The new inline editor script runs whenever the page is embedded in an iframe and accepts any message with type "INLINE_EDIT_CAPTURE_REQUEST". It then clones the DOM, renders it to a canvas, and sends a data URL back to the parent using postMessage("*") without checking e.origin or requiring a shared secret. Any attacker-controlled parent page can iframe the site and request screenshots/scroll data, bypassing the same‑origin policy and leaking whatever user-specific information is visible in the page.

title: Paymaster debug info exposed in owner approval errors
description: The commit adds an owner-approval debug mode that unconditionally sends the X-CV-Paymaster-Debug header whenever an approvalRunId is present, bypassing the PAYMASTER_DEBUG_HEADER_ENABLED gate. The paymaster handler returns verbose debug data (store addresses, expected vault/router config, validation context selectors/targets) when this header is set. The new owner-approval debug tag then appends those RPC details into error messages, and onboardingWallet explicitly surfaces them to end users. As a result, any authenticated user who triggers an owner-approval failure can extract internal paymaster configuration and validation context data that was previously suppressed in production.

title: CSV formula injection in new top-creators export
description: The newly added indexer script for exporting top creators (indexer/src/exportTopCreators.ts) assembles CSV rows from untrusted profile fields such as handle, display name, description, and website, then writes them to CSV using a simple quote-escaping helper. The helper only quotes commas/quotes/newlines and does not neutralize values starting with spreadsheet formula characters (=, +, -, @). A malicious creator could set their profile fields to a formula payload, and when the CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets by an operator, the formula executes (CSV injection), potentially exfiltrating data or triggering follow-on actions on the analyst’s machine.

title: useAccountMe cache persists across auth changes, leaking data
description: `useAccountMe` now calls `/api/accounts/me` with a Privy access token and stores the response in a module-level `cached` variable. When the user logs out, `useSafePrivyAccessToken` returns null and `fetchAccountMe` exits early without clearing the cache. Because the effect short-circuits when `cached` is already set, the hook continues to return the prior user’s `AccountSetupMe` (email, linked methods, canonical CSW address) to unauthenticated or newly authenticated users until a focus event or manual refresh clears it. This introduces a local information disclosure across account switches.

title: Raw paymaster/bundler errors now returned in user responses
description: The new error-wrapping path stores the original RPC/paymaster message as `causeMessage` and `submitUserOpOrRefuse` now prefers that message when building the user-facing `response`. This means unredacted backend errors (often containing internal diagnostics or hostnames) are surfaced to end users instead of the previous opaque code. An attacker can intentionally provoke UserOp failures and harvest these messages for reconnaissance.

title: useAccountMe cache can leak prior CSW after logout
description: The newly introduced useAccountMe hook caches the /api/accounts/me response at module scope and skips refetching whenever the cache is non-undefined. This cache is never tied to the SIWE session or cleared on sign-out. useCanonicalIdentity now derives cswAddress directly from accountMe.me, even when there is no active session. As a result, if a user signs out and another user signs in (or the same user signs out) without a full reload or focus refresh, the previous user's canonical CSW can remain visible in identity UI (and future consumers of useAccountMe could expose additional account fields). This is a stale-identity/info-leak issue on shared devices.

title: On-chain strategy deployment bypasses paid feature enforcement
description: The commit introduces a paid opt‑in model for Charm/Ajna/Solana strategies, but the on-chain deployment path does not enforce any proof of payment. `DeploymentBatcher.deployPhase3Strategies` only checks the caller is the vault owner and validates weight ranges; if a creator calls the batcher directly (or crafts a UserOp that reaches it), they can pass non‑zero weights and deploy paid strategies without ever activating or paying through the new API flows. This bypasses the intended paywall and can trigger paid‑only provisioning costs without authorization.

title: Trend reserve UserOp bypasses spend caps for zero-value deploys
description: The new Arch‑B trend reserve path builds a UserOp with valueWei=0 for TrendCoinFactory.deployTrendCoin and routes it through submitUserOpOrRefuse. That submitter only reserves daily spend and performs balance preflight when valueWei > 0. As a result, the new trend reserve path never consumes daily budget or caps, leaving only the per‑group 60‑second cooldown. An ADMIN/OWNER with command access can repeatedly reserve trends to trigger expensive contract deployments at sponsor expense, risking paymaster drain or service degradation. This exposure is new because the legacy path required a funded agent EOA, naturally throttling gas usage.

title: Arch B daily cap check is race-prone, enabling cap bypass
description: In the Arch B user operation submitter, daily caps are enforced by reading the current spend total and comparing it to the cap, then later incrementing the spend counter with a separate write. Because these two steps are not atomic, multiple concurrent requests can read the same spend value, pass the cap check, and then each reserve spend, resulting in the daily cap being exceeded. The underlying recordIssuerDailySpend function blindly increments spent_wei without verifying the cap, so there is no protection against this race. This defeats the intended per-profile daily limit and can permit more spending than configured.

title: Broad fallback regex can free valid referral codes
description: The commit replaces an exact fallback check with a broad `/^C[0-9A-Z]{1,4}$/` regex. This makes any 2–5 character C‑prefixed referral code eligible for automatic upgrade, even if it was intentionally assigned from a handle or email. When upgraded, the original code is removed with no tombstone/alias, so it becomes available for reuse. A malicious user can then register with a matching email local‑part or handle to claim that freed code and capture referrals previously attributed to the original owner.

title: Referrer lookup leaks data for non-public waitlist profiles
description: The added /api/waitlist/referrer endpoint looks up profiles solely by referral_code and returns display name plus points totals. Unlike the leaderboard, it does not restrict results to profiles with profile_completed_at set. Because referral codes are derived from guessable sources (email local parts, coin symbols, base36 IDs), an attacker can enumerate codes and retrieve display identifiers and points for profiles that are not yet public on the leaderboard, bypassing the intended privacy gate.

title: RPC proxy IP rate limits bypassable via spoofed headers
description: The commit changes client IP detection to always fall back to the `x-forwarded-for` header in production and adds logic in the RPC proxy to skip IP rate limiting when the resolved IP is `unknown`. Because `x-forwarded-for` is not validated as a trusted edge header, a client can supply an arbitrary value (or force `unknown` via a spoofed header) and either rotate IPs to bypass the per-IP limit or disable the IP limit entirely. Previously, production ignored `x-forwarded-for` and always enforced the IP bucket (even for `unknown`), preventing this abuse. This weakens abuse protections and can enable RPC proxy resource exhaustion or rate-limit evasion by authenticated users rotating principals.

title: Unhandled body_too_large errors in deploy handlers
description: readBoundedJsonObjectBody throws an exception when Vercel has already parsed the request body and the serialized size exceeds maxBytes. The updated deploy handlers call this helper without a try/catch, so oversized but otherwise valid JSON (still within the platform body limit) results in an unhandled exception and a 500 response. An attacker can repeatedly send oversized JSON to public endpoints like /deploy/smartWalletOwner to force error responses and reduce availability.

title: Inline wallet script makes window.ethereum writable early
description: The added inline script in index.html runs at document start and, when it detects a locked ethereum descriptor, redefines window.ethereum with configurable/writable=true. This bypasses the read-only protections that wallet extensions use to prevent provider spoofing and runs before other page scripts. As a result, any subsequent script (including third-party/supply‑chain script or XSS payload) can replace window.ethereum with a malicious proxy and intercept or alter wallet requests, enabling transaction/signature hijacking within the page context.

title: Unredacted conversation IDs now logged in AI chat runtime
description: The refactor removed use of the redaction helper and now logs params.groupId directly in multiple log statements. groupId values embed chat/channel identifiers (e.g., Telegram chat IDs, Discord channels), so writing them verbatim to logs exposes PII to log sinks/third‑party observability. This is a regression from the previous redacted logging and enables unintended information disclosure via logs.

title: SMART_WALLET mode bypasses owner-check fallback for XMTP
description: The updated XMTP identity resolution now prefers an account-context smart wallet address and, in SMART_WALLET mode, explicitly preserves that identity even if the on-chain owner check fails or is unavailable. This removes the previous safety fallback to the connected EOA when ownership cannot be proven. If a stale or cached smart-wallet address is present (e.g., from a previous session or a transient waitlist response) and the owner check fails due to RPC issues, the app can continue using the smart-wallet identity and potentially reopen an existing XMTP installation for that address without verifying ownership, exposing prior chat history or enabling impersonation from the same browser.

title: Unbounded on-chain identity cache enables memory DoS via public API
description: The new on-chain identity resolver keeps a module-level Map of cached profiles keyed by address. Although each entry has a TTL timestamp, expired entries are never removed, so the Map only grows. The public GET /api/portfolio/me?address=... path now calls resolveOnchainIdentityProfile for arbitrary addresses, meaning an unauthenticated attacker can request many unique addresses and force unbounded cache growth. Over time this can exhaust memory and crash or recycle the serverless instance, leading to a denial-of-service condition.

title: Chat display name truncation enables ENS/Basename spoofing
description: The commit now removes the .base.eth or .eth suffix from resolved ENS/Basename identifiers before caching and displaying them. This makes "alice.eth" and "alice.base.eth" both appear as "alice" in the chat UI. Because the UI no longer shows the full suffix, a malicious actor can register a similarly prefixed name to visually impersonate another user in conversation lists and message headers, increasing phishing/social‑engineering risk.

title: Canonical AlfaClub key routes render a blank loader
description: RootRouter now treats any path returned by `resolveAlfaClubCanonicalPath()` as a redirect target. The same commit added the canonical `/keys` and `/explore/keys` paths to that resolver. As a result, visiting `https://app.4626.fun/keys` or `https://app.4626.fun/explore/keys` never reaches the App routes that mount `AlfaClubHostApp`; RootRouter renders `AlfaClubHostRedirect` first. `AlfaClubHostRedirect` correctly avoids `window.location.replace()` when the target equals the current URL, but it still returns only `AppLoadingRegistrar`, so the page remains blank/loading permanently.

title: Wire-gas UserOps no longer self-bundle or use paymaster
description: Non-phase2_core deploy stages are now forced to DEPLOY_SESSION_PHASE2_WIRE_USEROP_GAS. That gas profile totals 3.6M, below the 12M self-bundle threshold, so createDeploySessionBundlerTransport forwards the UserOp to the upstream bundler instead of calling selfBundleUserOp. However the continue/advance paths construct and call the bundler without passing a paymaster to sendUserOperation. CDP cannot sponsor an already-signed UserOp unless paymaster data is included in the signed UserOp fields, so these wire-stage UserOps are sent without paymasterAndData and must be paid by the smart wallet or its EntryPoint deposit. Fresh deployment sessions generally rely on sponsorship/self-bundling rather than a pre-funded smart wallet, so phase1, phase2 pre-finalize/finalize, phase3, phase4, and cleanup fallback can stall with insufficient prefund/AA21-style failures. This is an availability/liveness regression, not an auth bypass or fund-theft issue.

title: Unbounded Solana ingest pagination enables relay DoS
description: The updated `drainSignaturesSinceWatermark` now defaults `maxPages` to `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` when callers omit it. The main caller, `ingestFinalizedLotteryLogs`, does omit `maxPages`, so each ingest run can page through the entire Solana program history until it finds the stored watermark or reaches the beginning. The function accumulates every signature in `newestFirst` and reverses the full array before processing any transaction. If the cursor is missing, stale, or far behind, or if an attacker cheaply creates a large number of finalized transactions involving the hook program, the worker can consume excessive memory/RPC time and repeatedly timeout or crash. This can prevent or significantly delay Solana lottery entry ingestion and relay, degrading lottery availability for legitimate users.

title: Agent canary plans predict the wrong ShareOFT address
description: In the newly added canary deploy-plan builder, `resolveVanityPlanLite` constructs `shareOftInitCode` with `DEPLOY_BYTECODE.CreatorShareOFT` regardless of `--vault-kind`. However, phase-1 calldata is built with `resolveDeployLanePhase1CodeIds(args.vaultKind)`, which selects `DEPLOY_BYTECODE.AgentShareOFT` for agent vaults. Since CREATE2 addresses depend on the creation bytecode hash, an agent canary plan predicts `expected.shareOFT` using CreatorShareOFT while the batcher deploys AgentShareOFT from the provided code ID. Downstream expected-address derivation uses the bad `shareOftInitCode`, and the batcher later checks phase-2 params against the phase-1 state, so the agent plan can revert or become stuck after phase 1. This is an operational crash/availability bug in the new canary helper, not a direct remote security vulnerability.

title: Unquoted glob breaks validate:contracts script
description: The commit adds `validate:contracts` as `bash -c 'cd .. && forge test --no-match-path test/vault/strategies/CreatorOVaultStrategies.Rebalance.*'`. Because the pattern is inside the inner Bash command and is not quoted, Bash expands it to every matching Rebalance test file in the repository. Foundry then receives only the first expanded path as the value for `--no-match-path`, with the remaining expanded filenames as extra positional arguments, which can make the shortcut fail outright or fail to exclude the intended Rebalance suite. This is a validation-process bug, not a runtime application or smart-contract vulnerability.

title: Direct room images are blocked by production CSP
description: RoomDiscoveryTray now assigns `room.imageUrl` directly to the ``. The previous same-origin proxy path would have been covered by `img-src 'self'`. The updated behavior test asserts direct rendering of `https://project.storage.supabase.co/room-1659` and says CSP allowlists the room image domains, but `frontend/vercel.json` only allowlists a single concrete Supabase project host (`https://volvarrdooikeahzzvqc.storage.supabase.co`) and not `https://project.storage.supabase.co` or `https://*.storage.supabase.co`. In production, browsers enforcing the CSP will refuse those direct image loads, causing remote tray artwork to fail and fall back.

title: Broken audit summary runbook link
description: The new Ops harden order link in `docs/audits/aristotle/ve4626-curve-boost/ARISTOTLE_SUMMARY.md` uses `../../operations/lottery-canary-checklist-2026-07.md`. From that file's directory, this resolves to `docs/audits/operations/lottery-canary-checklist-2026-07.md`, which does not exist. The existing checklist is at `docs/operations/lottery-canary-checklist-2026-07.md`, so the relative link should go up three levels (`../../../operations/...`). This is a documentation/navigation bug only.

title: Zora owner-install uses wagmi config with no connectors
description: WaitlistLegacyOwnerInstall now always wraps its inner owner-install controller in WaitlistMessagingWalletProviders. When preferBaseAppPath is false, it passes connectTrack='zora-owner-install'. createWaitlistMessagingWagmiConfig deliberately only installs a Coinbase connector for 'base-app-direct'; all other tracks, including 'zora-owner-install', get an empty connector list. The owner-install controller then reads connectedAddress and wagmiConnections from wagmi, but its Connect CSW owner wallet button calls Privy's connectWallet rather than wagmi connectAsync. As a result, in the non-Base-App Zora owner-install lane, the Privy wallet may connect while wagmi remains disconnected/empty, so connectedOnchainEoaOwner stays null and the Enable 4626 signing path remains disabled or later fails with no matching wagmi account. This is an availability/UX regression for owner installation, not an authentication bypass or funds-at-risk issue.

title: Vercel env sync aborts after valid new env additions
description: The new upsert_env implementation backgrounds `vercel env add`, writes output to `/tmp/vercel-env-add.log`, and only considers the operation successful if that log contains `Overrode Environment Variable`. Vercel env variables that do not already exist are validly created with output such as `Added Environment Variable ...`; those successful first-time additions do not match the grep, so the function reaches the failure path and returns 1. Because the script runs with `set -e`, this aborts the v1.18.0 Vercel env sync before redeploying. This is especially likely for the CREATOR_* aliases added in the same commit because they are new variables.

title: v1.17 manifest omits impairment aux bytecode
description: The committed manifest ends without entries for OVaultImpairmentClaims and OVaultRecoveryEscrow, even though the frontend deploy bytecode generator emits both and buildImpairmentAuxPlan uses them to deploy a fresh impairment claims/recovery escrow pair for each vault. A local comparison of DEPLOY_BYTECODE against the manifest found the missing entries: OVaultImpairmentClaims, 4964 bytes, keccak 0xe33770e148c097ae083e66e0da90705ad10b00c7300d963604c2ab70b1fd960c; and OVaultRecoveryEscrow, 1471 bytes, keccak 0xe80c797348061cab3f363e030594cd9d84f10dc037d5bec567a835ff40ff52be. This does not appear to be directly exploitable because the impairment aux pair is deployed from frontend bytecode via the permissionless CREATE2 deployer rather than from this manifest or the UniversalBytecodeStore. However, it is an operational/release-verification bug: manifest-based verification can pass without attesting the emergency recovery auxiliary bytecode used by every vault.

title: Share-mesh cutover uses an ABI not in the codebase
description: The new cutover scripts import and instantiate `DeploymentBatcherShareMeshHelper` and call `DeploymentBatcher.shareMeshHelper()`. However, the repository's `contracts/shared/deploy/batchers/DeploymentBatcher.sol` still defines `DeploymentBatcherUniV4Helper public uniV4Helper` and wires helpers through an `_uniV4Helper` parameter. There is no checked-in `DeploymentBatcherShareMeshHelper` contract or `shareMeshHelper()` getter in that source. This makes the new deployment/cutover tooling inconsistent with the contract ABI it imports. In practice, these scripts cannot compile against the current source, or the frontend/deployment preflight will query the wrong helper getter depending on which on-chain shell is used. This can block the v1.16.1 cutover and new vault launches, but I did not find a direct exploitable fund-loss or authorization bypass in this commit.

title: Generated contract SUMMARY links are broken
description: In docs/_generated/contracts/src/SUMMARY.md, the PayoutRouter and VaultShareBurnStream entries were changed from the existing generated docs location under contracts/utilities/routers/... to contracts/creator/revenue/.... The source Solidity contracts do exist under contracts/creator/revenue, but the generated documentation files in docs/_generated/contracts/src were not moved or regenerated into that matching path. As a result, SUMMARY.md links for these eight entries resolve to missing files, while the actual generated pages remain under docs/_generated/contracts/src/contracts/utilities/routers/.... This is a documentation/navigation regression, not a runtime or security vulnerability.

title: Thread fallback duplicates daily brief parent posts
description: The new threaded posting path sends the compact parent message before it knows whether replies can be threaded. If sendAlfaClubRoomText returns a null messageId, sendDailyBriefToCommandRooms falls back by sending the full digest as a separate flat message. However, the parent was already posted successfully. sendAlfaClubRoomText explicitly returns messageId: null for JWT HTTP fallback and WebSocket lanes, so any deployment without a bot-token message ID will consistently post both the parent pulse and the flat digest. This is a reliability/spam bug rather than a security vulnerability; it can clutter rooms and may confuse digest accounting, but it does not bypass authentication or expose new privileged data.

title: Dry-run RPC unauthenticated fallback is unreachable
description: In the RPC proxy, the new dry-run logic computes allowUnauthenticatedLocalFork and then tries to use a synthetic principal via `readRequestPrincipalAddress(req) ?? ...`. However, `readRequestPrincipalAddress` is typed and implemented to return a string, returning `''` when there is no session or SIWA principal. Because `''` is not nullish, the `??` fallback is skipped, leaving `principalAddress` empty and causing the existing 401 path to run. This means the newly introduced unauthenticated local-fork dry-run behavior is effectively dead code. The bug fails closed and does not create an auth bypass, so it is not security-impacting.

title: Docs repo links are pinned to main
description: The commit adds automatic linking for inline-code repository paths, but the shared helper hardcodes `https://github.com/wenakita/4626/blob/main`. This bypasses the repository's existing DOCS_GITHUB_REF convention for release or branch-specific documentation builds. As a result, docs generated for a release branch or historical commit will silently link readers to source files on the mutable `main` branch, which can cause auditors, operators, or users to inspect the wrong code version. The plugin is enabled in Docusaurus, so every matched inline-code source path rendered by the docs site is affected.

title: Solana hook setup passes incompatible address format
description: The commit wires /api/keeper/solana/provision-creator to call the Solana provisioner's /setup-creator endpoint. The request body uses params.creatorToken and shareOft directly, which are normalized EVM addresses such as 0x + 40 hex characters. The provisioner passes those values unchanged as --hub-creator-coin and --hub-share-token to kpr/scripts/solana/deploy/setup-creator-full.ts. That script calls hexToBytes32(), which rejects anything except 64 hex characters. As a result, normal post-deploy hook provisioning fails before initializeCreator runs, leaving the required Token-2022 hook lane uncreated. The handler records the failed hook attempt and then continues to Meteora pool creation, so the deployment can proceed while the hook lane remains missing.

title: Legacy batcher monitoring query points to wrong file
description: The updated current batcher Dune query now filters the v1.14.1 batcher address, which is consistent with the current address documentation. However, the newly added comment says the legacy v1.11.2-pipe-a shell at 0xa99058... should be monitored with 02-legacy-batcher-tx-volume.sql. That referenced query only tracks the older AKITA/pre-pipe-a batcher at 0x16aEA859..., and there is no remaining Dune query in the directory for the 0xa99058... batcher. Operators following the comment would lose visibility into the v1.11.2-pipe-a batcher’s historical transaction volume.

title: Docs fallback error does not fail production builds
description: When `DOCS_REQUIRE_MANUAL_SOURCE=1` is set and the docs sync falls back to a bundled snapshot, the script records an error in `stats.errors`. However, `sync-docs.mjs` only calls `process.exit(1)` when `STRICT_MODE` is enabled. The new `build:production` command sets `DOCS_REQUIRE_MANUAL_SOURCE=1` but still invokes `build:slim`, whose `sync-docs` call is not strict. As a result, the sync step can complete with errors and return success, allowing the subsequent Docusaurus build to proceed with stale bundled docs instead of failing as intended.

title: Docs build imports undeclared remark dependency
description: The new wrapTables remark plugin has a runtime import from unist-util-visit and is enabled from docusaurus.config.ts. The docs-site package uses pnpm and its package.json does not list unist-util-visit in dependencies or devDependencies, so the app is relying on a transitive dependency from Docusaurus/MDX packages. Under pnpm's isolated dependency layout, project code generally cannot import undeclared transitive packages, so a clean docs build/start can fail with a module-resolution error when Docusaurus loads the config. Type-only imports from unified/mdast may also fail in strict typechecking unless their type packages are declared. This is an availability/build reliability issue for the docs site, not a protocol/security vulnerability.

title: Waitlist sub-account chat eligibility removed
description: The waitlist XMTP chat authorization logic previously allowed a user to join through a registered Base App sub-account when WAITLIST_SUBACCOUNT_FLOW_ENABLED was enabled and profiles.base_sub_account was distinct from the canonical CSW. This commit removes the sub-account execution track from WaitlistChatExecutionTrack, stops passing the feature flag into the eligibility resolver, and leaves only the legacy parent-CSW owner-install path. As a result, users who completed the sub-account registration flow but do not have the embedded EOA installed as a direct parent CSW owner will now be classified as none-yet and blocked with embedded_owner_not_installed. The join/resync handlers still contain sub-account branches, showing the route contract still expects this path to exist, but it is now unreachable. This is an authorization/availability regression for a gated chat feature and may also create TypeScript no-overlap comparison errors during server typechecking.

title: Chat provider crashes on app routes without PrivyProvider
description: This commit replaces the shared Layout's XmtpChatProvider with ChatProviderWithSessionRepair. The wrapper immediately calls useXmtpSessionRepair, which immediately calls usePrivy. However, the /explore route family is rendered under LazyAccessBoundary, which provides WalletProviders and AccessStateProvider but not PrivyProvider; PrivyProvider is only introduced by a sibling LazyPrivyBoundary used for other app routes. As a result, visiting an accepted app /explore route with chat enabled can throw the standard 'usePrivy must be used within PrivyProvider' error and take down the React route/UI. An attacker could trigger a client-side availability failure by linking an authenticated user to an affected route. The issue can be fixed by only mounting ChatProviderWithSessionRepair inside PrivyProvider-backed route trees, by wrapping all chat-enabled app layouts with PrivyProvider, or by making the repair hook safely no-op when Privy context is absent and falling back to the bare XmtpChatProvider.

title: Stale token reset skipped when invalid token is non-null
description: The new probeStalePrivyTokenSession implementation treats any non-empty getAccessToken() result as proof that the session is not stale. However, the stale-token error classifier includes server-side invalid-token and expired-session errors. In those cases, requestBootstrap can fail because the server rejects the token, while getAccessToken() continues returning the same invalid token string. The newly changed catch paths then call the probe, receive false, and avoid resetStaleAuthenticatedPrivySession(). The background retry path eventually times out instead of clearing the bad Privy session, and manual retry can repeat the same failure. This is a client-side auth liveness/UX regression rather than an authorization bypass, because server-side token verification still prevents access with an invalid token.

title: Trade lifecycle connectors ignore flip/add starts
description: This is a frontend-only visualization regression in `Positions.tsx`. The surrounding code models flips as resetting the position entry price, meaning a flip is also the start of a new lifecycle for the opposite side. Before this commit, `entry`, `add`, and `flip` were all treated as open-family events for connector range tracking. The new code records only `action === 'entry'`, so visible lifecycles that begin with a flip, or with an add when the original entry is outside the recent timeline window, are not tracked and their connector lines can disappear. This does not affect contract execution, authentication, custody, or backend authorization.

title: Catch-all routing breaks social preview debug path
description: The commit registers `social-preview-debug` in the catch-all API route map. The catch-all dispatcher treats any `req.query.path` as the API subpath to route to, and the Vercel rewrite also uses `?path=$1` for `/api/(.*)`. However, the social preview debug endpoint's public API requires callers to pass a `path` query parameter containing the page path to test, e.g. `/api/social-preview-debug?path=/explore/creators/...`. After this refactor, that parameter collides with the catch-all routing parameter. Depending on how Vercel merges the route rewrite and original query string, the request is either dispatched to the wrong API subpath or the handler receives the route subpath instead of the page path. This makes the debug endpoint unreliable or unusable when accessed through its real deployed route. The tests import the handler directly, so they bypass the catch-all dispatcher and do not catch this regression.

title: Retired Ethos functions leave callers broken
description: The new retirement migration removes public.refresh_all_ethos_chart_views() and public.run_zora_owner_ethos_projection(integer). However, an earlier migration schedules two pg_cron jobs that still execute SELECT public.refresh_all_ethos_chart_views(), and the hot Ethos sync handler still calls public.run_zora_owner_ethos_projection(20000) in its projection fallback path. The migration does not unschedule the old cron jobs or update the fallback caller. After deployment, those cron jobs will fail every day with missing-function errors, and the hot-sync fallback will silently stop performing its intended repair because the error is caught and logged as query_failed.

title: Daily Ethos snapshots can retain stale scores
description: The migration changes snapshot_creator_ethos_daily() to insert/update only projection rows with ethos_score IS NOT NULL, and performs only a one-time cleanup of historical NULL-score rows. The projection refresh path can update creator_ethos_projection.ethos_score to NULL and then call snapshot_creator_ethos_daily(). In that case, any existing snapshot row for CURRENT_DATE is no longer updated to NULL or removed, so charts or reports based on creator_ethos_daily_snapshots can continue to display an obsolete scored value. This is a data-integrity bug rather than a security vulnerability, based on the reviewed call paths.

title: Deploy route can render smart-wallet hook without provider
description: SmartWalletsRouteProvider now returns its children without SmartWalletsProvider whenever Privy is ready but the user is not Privy-authenticated. The /deploy/vault route is wrapped in SmartWalletRoute, and DeployVaultMain unconditionally calls useSmartWallets during render before it reaches the UI branch that shows the "Sign in to Deploy" button for unauthenticated Privy users. For Privy smart-wallet libraries that require useSmartWallets to be under SmartWalletsProvider, this renders the hook outside its provider and trips the DeployVault error boundary instead of allowing the user to sign in. This is an availability/regression bug rather than a security vulnerability.

title: Room-history network failures now return successful ticks
description: The new timeout handling path returns an early tick result instead of throwing. However, fetchRoomHistory already wraps every fetch exception as room_history_failed:timeout, not only AbortController timeouts. As a result, DNS failures, TLS/proxy failures, connection resets, and real upstream outages are all treated as quiet timeout transients. Even after the sustained threshold is reached, the code only logs a warning and still returns a normal tick result. runAlfaClubChatBridgeTickOnce then returns ok: true, and the cron endpoint responds HTTP 200 with success: true. This can hide a broken bridge from HTTP/status-based monitoring and cause chat commands not to be processed until history fetching recovers. This is an availability/observability regression rather than an exploitable auth, funds, or data-confidentiality issue.

title: Preseed normalization defeats fresh deploy namespaces
description: The commit adds normalizePreseedBaseVersion(), which reduces any string beginning with v<major>.<minor>.<patch> to only that semver prefix. matchesPreseedIdentity() then compares the manifest plan's baseVersion to this normalized value. When the AKITA preseed plan matches, lookupPreseededVanityVersionPlan() returns the manifest deploymentVersion v1.14.0-vqvt, and resolveDeployVanityPlan() uses that returned version as deploymentVersionUsed. DeployVault then writes expectedDeploymentVersion back into the active deploymentVersion state. As a result, user/operator namespaces such as v1.14.0-dryrun, v1.14.0-retry-1, or even v1.14.0foo can be silently snapped back to v1.14.0-vqvt for the preseeded identity/default vanity path. This contradicts the fresh-namespace and local dry-run isolation semantics documented in the same commit, and can cause retry/dry-run deployments to collide with the already-grounded namespace instead of using a fresh deterministic slate.

title: shareTokenLogo now disables creator token avatars
description: The updated shareTokenLogo helper ignores its address and chainId arguments and always returns an empty string. New and existing token-label paths use this helper as the logo URL for creator/share tokens. The same commit also adds noFallback to TokenAvatar in the selector rows; when no logo candidates exist, TokenAvatar returns null. As a result, pinned creator tokens and creator-token selector entries can render without any avatar instead of using the intended generated/raw token image or fallback initials. This is a UI/UX regression rather than an exploitable security issue.

title: InvalidWeight mapping is shadowed by generic revert handling
description: The commit adds detection for InvalidWeight reverts from rebalanceStrategies(), but executeVaultRebalanceStrategies checks isKnownRebalanceExecutionRevert before isKnownRebalanceInvalidWeightRejection. The generic predicate matches common viem revert text such as `contract function "rebalancestrategies" reverted` or `execution reverted`, which will also be present for many custom-error reverts carrying the InvalidWeight selector/name. As a result, real InvalidWeight failures are likely wrapped as `rebalance_strategies_reverted` before the new invalid-weight branch is reached. The API handler has a mapping for `rebalance_strategies_invalid_weight`, but the normal executor path will usually not emit that code. This is an operational correctness bug affecting skip reasons/monitoring and remediation, not an apparent security vulnerability.

title: Skipped rebalance responses are retried as failures
description: This commit adds health-gate/no-strategy/unauthorized/gas-rejected skip paths for `/api/keeper/rebalance-strategies`, but each skip response is encoded as HTTP 200 with `success:false`. The keeper job runner enqueues this endpoint as an internal API job and its `callInternalApi` helper requires both `response.ok` and `json.success === true`; otherwise it throws. Therefore, the newly added skip responses are not treated as completed skipped work. They are retried and can eventually fail the job/control-plane stage. This can cause queue churn, noisy failures, and unnecessary keeper capacity consumption for normal states such as vaults with no strategies or a configured health-gate block. The fix is to either return `success:true` with `data.status: 'skipped'` for non-error skip outcomes, or update the internal job runner to explicitly accept documented skipped envelopes.

title: Ethos sync cron can hang on DB acquisition failure
description: In the updated Ethos canonical sync handler, `getDbForCron()` is awaited before the inner `try/catch`. If that call rejects, `runTickPromise` rejects. The surrounding timeout wrapper attaches a `.catch()` that clears the timeout but does not resolve or reject the outer Promise, so `await new Promise(...)` can wait forever until the serverless platform kills the request. The previous implementation could fail the request directly; the new wrapper converts this failure mode into a hang. Move DB acquisition inside the inner try/catch or resolve an error response in the outer `.catch()` instead of only clearing the timeout.

title: V2 breakout hero clearance is computed but not rendered
description: In premium-v2 token icon rendering, the commit moved hero breakout clearance to occur after the breakout layer is finalized. However, the code pushes the original `heroLayer` buffer into `overlays` before calling `eraseHeroUnderBreakoutLayer`. Since `compositeStep(heroLayer, 'over')` stores the current Buffer object, later reassigning `heroLayer` to a new Buffer does not update the already-created overlay entry. As a result, the rendered image still composites the uncleared hero layer, and the intended double-hat/face removal does not take effect. This appears to be a correctness/quality regression rather than a security issue.

title: Partial digest posts suppress retries to missed rooms
description: The new multi-room sender intentionally continues after per-room send failures and returns success as long as at least one room was posted. `runAlfaClubDailyBrief` then records dispatch rows only for the rooms that succeeded. However, before sending, it still calls `hasDailyBriefDispatchForSnapshot(snapshotTs)`, which checks only whether any room has a dispatch for that snapshot. As a result, a transient failure for one command room can be made permanent for that snapshot: once another room has been recorded, the next scheduled run with `forceSend` disabled returns `skippedDuplicate: true` and never attempts the unposted room. This was not a correctness issue when only one reachable room was posted, but it becomes a multi-room delivery bug after this commit.

title: Custom telemetry rate envs are ignored
description: Before this change, shouldSampleEvent(tableName, key, rateEnv) used rateEnv to resolve both the table-specific environment variable and the global fallback. The new getTelemetrySampleRate() helper hard-codes TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE, and shouldSampleEvent() calls it without passing rateEnv. This silently breaks any caller or external/internal future use that relies on an alternate sampling namespace. I did not find any current in-repository caller passing the third argument, so this is not an active security vulnerability in the checked-out code, but it is an introduced behavioral regression in an exported helper.

title: Eliza bootstrap masks failed main module startup
description: The Docker entrypoint now starts server/agents/eliza/bootstrap.ts, and Railway is configured to consider /healthz as the deployment health check. bootstrap.ts returns HTTP 200 for /healthz while the main Eliza module is still evaluating. If the dynamic import of ./index.ts fails during module evaluation, the catch handler only logs the error and does not exit the process or change /healthz to a failing status. This can leave a deployment marked healthy even though no keeper/agent runtime is running. Because this repository assumes one Railway primary replica, such a masked startup failure can cause a prolonged automation outage until operators manually inspect logs or hit /readyz.

title: Probe can claim welcomes before validating send
description: The commit adds a local/operator script for probing and optionally sending Hermit room welcome messages. I did not find an externally exposed security vulnerability: the new file is an ops script, arguments are validated or parameterized for SQL, and it does not print secret values. However, the --send flow has an operational correctness bug. When --send is passed, the script first inserts the room_welcome_sent ledger claim and only afterwards validates that the room is allowed and that the AlfaClub send path has usable credentials, then attempts to send. If the later validation or send fails, the ledger row remains and future bridge/probe runs will treat the wallet as already welcomed even though no welcome was posted. The missing-env check is also ineffective for websocket credentials because readAlfaClubChatBridgeFlags always supplies a default websocketUrl, so a no-credential --send attempt can still claim the ledger before sendAlfaClubRoomText throws alfaclub_jwt_missing.

title: Telemetry retention migration is nonfunctional
description: The existing cleanup_log_retention function has 5 integer parameters with defaults and is called by cron as public.cleanup_log_retention() with no arguments. This migration adds 13 more defaulted parameters, creating an 18-argument overload rather than replacing the 5-argument function. The migration then attempts to REVOKE/GRANT a 17-argument function signature, which does not match the function it just created and will fail on PostgreSQL. The comment saying the existing cron job will automatically pick up the new parameters is therefore incorrect: either the migration aborts, or the database is left with overloaded default-argument functions where a zero-argument call is ambiguous/not the intended target. Additionally, several new DELETE statements reference created_at on tables whose schema uses updated_at, last_updated, or snapshot_ts, so the new cleanup body would fail at runtime even if the signature issue were fixed.

title: Bootstrap health check can mask fatal Hermit startup failure
description: During bootstrap, the minimal listener now returns 200 for `/healthz` before `index.ts` has successfully loaded. If the dynamic import of `index.ts` fails, the catch block logs the failure but deliberately keeps the bootstrap server running. Railway is configured to use `/healthz` as its healthcheck path, so this failure mode can leave a deployment permanently healthy from Railway's perspective while the real health server, AlfaClub chat bridge, and token refresher never start. `/readyz` would still return 503, but it is not the configured Railway healthcheck.

title: Risk watcher state declarations accidentally removed
description: The healthcheck changes replaced the prior declarations of `isShuttingDown`, `lastSuccessfulTick`, and `lastTickStatus` with only `lastError` and `consecutiveFailures`. The rest of the script still reads and writes the removed variables. TypeScript will report unresolved names, and if run through `tsx` without typechecking, normal continuous execution reaches `while (!isShuttingDown)` and throws a `ReferenceError`. The tick and healthcheck paths also reference `lastSuccessfulTick` and `lastTickStatus`, so `--once`/healthcheck execution can also fail. This makes the Railway watcher restart-loop or stop monitoring, defeating the operational alerting that the commit intended to harden.

title: Railway watcher Docker build cannot find source file
description: The updated README instructs operators to set Railway's Root Directory to `scripts/ops/1659-risk-watcher`, and the Dockerfile then runs `COPY 1659-risk-watcher.ts ./`. However, the actual watcher source remains at `scripts/ops/1659-risk-watcher.ts`, which is a sibling of the Docker context directory, not inside it. Docker cannot copy files outside the build context, so following the new deployment instructions will fail the image build with a missing `1659-risk-watcher.ts` source. This is an availability/operations bug for the monitoring worker rather than an exploitable security vulnerability.

title: 1659 keeper risk monitor integration is nonfunctional
description: The commit claims to add end-to-end keeper_jobs integration for the 1659 HYPE risk watcher, but several introduced wiring errors prevent the monitor from executing in the managed keeper path. `enqueue-recurring.ts` creates jobs with kind `1659_hype_risk_monitor`, while the existing keeper job runner only claims `internal_api` and `noop` jobs, so these jobs will remain pending and never be processed. Even if the kind were changed, the intended path `/api/keeper/jobs/1659-risk-monitor` is not added to `frontend/api/_handlers/_routes.ts`, so the catch-all API router will not dispatch to the new handler. Additionally, both the new API handler and enqueue script use relative imports that resolve to non-existent paths (`frontend/scripts/...` and `scripts/frontend/...` respectively). Finally, the shared watcher module invokes `main()` at top level, so importing it as a library would start the continuous watcher loop instead of only exposing `run1659RiskTick`. Together these issues make the alerting/monitoring workflow unreliable or unavailable.

title: Owner-install pending state clears before completion
description: The commit wires the modern waitlist owner-install hook to report submit phases into useAccountSetupController. The controller then treats any non-idle phase as ownerInstallInProgress, but a new auto-clear effect clears that state whenever ownerApprovalReady is true. ownerApprovalReady is derived from connectedOwnerReady plus an available signer client; it can already be true before submitting the install, because the user must often have the current CSW owner/Base App signer connected to start the flow. As soon as handleSubmitUserOp sets the phase to preflight, the controller can clear the phase/hash before the wallet_sendCalls prompt or bundle confirmation completes. The AccountSetupWorkspaceView relies on ownerInstallInProgress/pendingOwnerInstallHash to show the waiting banner and suppress normal action panels, so clearing it early can expose the Submit UI again and allow duplicate owner-install attempts, confusing status, and wasted gas.

title: Payout harvest kill switch misses standalone workflow
description: This commit documents and configures KPR_PAYOUT_ROUTER_HARVEST_ENABLED=0 as the way to disable Railway KPR direct payout-router harvesting when Vercel keeper_jobs is the primary payout executor. However, the actual guard was added only to kpr/workflows/4626.workflow.ts. The repository also exposes and routes a normal standalone process via `pnpm start:payout-router-harvest` / `tsx runner.ts payout-router-harvest`, and that handler still calls executePayoutRouterHarvest() without checking the new flag. Operators following the new runbook can therefore believe KPR harvesting is disabled while a standalone Railway/KPR payout-harvest process continues to claim, convert, queue, and checkpoint the same routers as Vercel. This does not appear to enable attacker-controlled fund theft, but it can reintroduce the duplicate-writer races the commit intended to prevent, causing reverted duplicate transactions, keeper gas loss, noisy errors, and payout automation instability. The flag should be enforced in the standalone workflow as well, or preferably inside executePayoutRouterHarvest() so every entrypoint shares the same kill switch.

title: Hermit X cross-post captions are no longer uniquified
description: For Hermit media cross-posts, the previous helper appended stable uniqueness data such as meme id, media filename, and a UTC timestamp before posting to X. This commit removes that helper and changes buildHermitXPostPayload to use truncateWithEllipsis(caption, 280) directly. Because X rejects duplicate tweet text, especially with the same media, repeated /gmeow outputs that produce the same caption and GIF can fail instead of being cross-posted. The duplicate error is handled gracefully as a skipped post, so this is a reliability/availability regression rather than an authentication or data-exposure vulnerability.

title: Access-token staleness check reads wrong env var
description: The commit adds dbEnvStaleness to the AlfaClub auth-health snapshot so operators can detect when DB-backed tokens are older than the Vercel environment fallback. However, readAuthHealthSnapshot reads the access-token fallback from process.env.ALFACLUB_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN, while the actual Privy refresher uses ALFACLUB_CHAT_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN. As a result, if the real access-token env fallback is newer than the DB row, the new health check will treat the env access token as absent and will not emit db_lags_env for access-token staleness. This undermines the intended outage-detection guard and can leave operators with a false healthy/complete snapshot during token recovery. This is an operational availability/monitoring bug rather than an attacker-exploitable security issue.

title: Token rotation runbook uses wrong Privy env vars
description: The commit adds a canonical token rotation runbook and links to it from other operations docs. In that new runbook, the Privy bootstrap environment variables are documented without the `CHAT_` component. The production refresher does not read those names: it falls back only to `ALFACLUB_CHAT_PRIVY_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `ALFACLUB_CHAT_PRIVY_REFRESH_TOKEN`. An operator following the new runbook would successfully update the DB if they use the admin endpoint, but the Vercel bootstrap env mirror would be ineffective. During recovery cases where the DB row is absent, stale, or has to be rebuilt from env, the refresher would still see missing/stale bootstrap tokens and the AlfaClub bridge could remain unavailable.

title: Eliza /bridge alias is not dispatched
description: The new /bridge alias was added to parseSubcommand() in the Eliza AlfaClub plugin, and tests assert that parseSubcommand('/bridge') maps to status. However, the Eliza action's validate() function remains unchanged and returns true only when the message starts with /alfa. In ElizaOS runtimes that rely on validate() before invoking the handler, /bridge and /bridge status will be rejected before parseSubcommand() runs. The deterministic Telegram/AlfaClub command path has its own registry update, but the Eliza plugin path is inconsistent and the advertised alias is dead there.

title: Zora swaps hard-fail on preflight RPC errors
description: sendCoinbaseSmartWalletUserOperation now calls assertZoraRouterCallExecutesFromCsw for every Zora Universal Router call immediately before submission, outside the existing skipPreflightSimulation guard. The helper performs a production Base RPC eth_call and catches all failures, not just EVM reverts. Non-revert failures such as RPC timeout, rate limiting, provider outage, or malformed provider responses are rethrown as if the Zora swap would revert on-chain. This makes swap submission depend on an extra read RPC even when the caller requested preflight simulation to be skipped, causing an availability regression for valid Zora swaps.

title: skipLocalFork can still route Base reads to the fork
description: This commit adds /api/rpc?skipLocalFork=1 and a production Base read client intended to bypass the local Anvil dry-run fork for live Permit2 nonce and Coinbase Smart Wallet owner-index reads. However, getRpcUrls() only avoids prepending resolveLocalDryRunRpcUrl(); it does not remove the same local fork URL when it is already present in the chain RPC environment variables. The dry-run helper explicitly copies DEPLOY_DRY_RUN_LOCAL_RPC_URL into BASE_READ_RPC_URL and BASE_LOGS_RPC_URL, so getRpcUrls('base', { skipLocalFork: true }) can still return the local fork as the first upstream. As a result, Permit2 nonce, bytecode, and owner lookup reads that are supposed to reflect live Base may still read fork state and produce stale or incorrect signatures/owner indexes, leading to failed Zora CSW swap submissions in dry-run/live-submit mixed environments.

title: Zora trade quote proxy rejects valid quote responses
description: In `fetchZoraTradeQuote`, the new code parses the upstream Zora `/quote` response into `raw` and immediately requires `raw.success` to be boolean true or string "true". If the field is absent, `String(raw.success ?? '')` becomes an empty string and the function throws `Zora quote API returned an error` before checking whether `raw.call.target` and `raw.call.data` are present. Other code paths in this repository that call the same Zora quote endpoint still parse it as a raw quote object and validate `payload.call`, which indicates this endpoint's successful response shape is not an ApiEnvelope. As a result, authenticated users using `/api/zora/tradeQuote` can no longer obtain executable Zora trade calldata from otherwise valid upstream responses.

title: Unthrottled public Dune API execution endpoint
description: The commit exposes analytics/dune through the API router and implements it as a public GET endpoint. After only checking the HTTP method and DUNE_API_KEY configuration, the handler executes Dune SQL. The probe path is especially problematic: /api/analytics/dune?probe=1 executes SELECT 1 on every request, is explicitly uncached, and waits up to 30 seconds. Metric requests are cached only after a successful execution and have no in-flight de-duplication, so a burst of concurrent cache misses can trigger many medium-performance Dune executions before the cache is populated. Because executeDuneSql attaches the server-side DUNE_API_KEY to each Dune request, any network attacker can burn Dune API quota/credits and tie up Vercel/serverless workers. The endpoint should add a per-IP or durable rate limit, cache or disable public probes, restrict probes to admin/internal callers, add in-flight request coalescing, and use fetch timeouts/abort signals.

title: SBF build check misses settle_fees validation
description: This commit adds scripts/build-sbf.sh and wires it as the recommended creator-share-hook build path. The script is described as building relay_entries / settle_fees bytecode, and the runbook requires canonical instruction strings to be present before mainnet deployment. However, the automated post-build gate only checks for relay_entries and rejects legacy drain/flush strings. If a malformed or accidentally changed program still contains relay_entries but omits settle_fees, this script would exit successfully, allowing operators to deploy bytecode that breaks keeper fee settlement. This is an operational integrity/availability bug rather than a remotely exploitable vulnerability in the deployed program logic.

title: Safe rejection list mode requires a private key
description: In frontend/scripts/ops/reject-stale-safe-transactions.ts, the script normalizes the Safe owner private key during initial argument parsing, before checking whether the caller requested --list or --dry-run. However, --list exits before any transaction creation/execution, and --dry-run only prints planned nonce rejections. Neither path needs a private key. As written, running the documented --list command without PRIVATE_KEY/SAFE_OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY fails with 'Missing private key'. This is an introduced operational bug rather than an externally exploitable vulnerability, but it can block read-only queue inspection and may lead operators to expose Safe owner keys unnecessarily for non-mutating commands.

title: Miniapp URL fix is lost during HTML generation
description: The changed fc:miniapp/fc:frame launch URLs in frontend/index.html and frontend/app.html are not the source of truth. The project's predev/prebuild scripts regenerate these files from frontend/html-shells templates. Those templates still emit APP_BASE_URL_TRAILING, which resolves to shared/site-config.json's marketing URL https://4626.fun rather than appUrl https://app.4626.fun. As a result, `node frontend/scripts/generate-html-shells.mjs --check` reports index.html and app.html as stale, and a normal build will overwrite the committed app-host launch URL back to the old marketing-host URL. This is a functional/release correctness bug, not a security vulnerability.

title: Charm keeper rebalance authorization regression
description: The updated rebalance executors now only allow direct EOA rebalancing when the keeper address matches rebalanceDelegate, or route through the protocol treasury Safe when manager is the protocol treasury. This drops previously supported authorization paths. In kpr/actions/charm-rebalance-manager.action.ts, the code still reads and validates charmKeeper, but keeperCanDirectlyRebalance ignores the case where charmKeeper equals the keeper address, so such vaults are skipped as unauthorized. In frontend/server/keepr/strategyActionExecutor.ts, the previous direct path allowed managerAddress == keeperAddress, but the new code only checks delegateAddress == keeperAddress unless the manager is the protocol treasury. This can break rebalancing for valid Charm vault configurations and leave LP ranges stale, potentially reducing strategy performance. I did not find an externally exploitable authentication bypass, fund theft path, or secret leak in the commit.

title: Backfill script loads .env too late for The Graph key
description: The script is intended to run with DATABASE_URL and graph/Zora API keys from frontend/.env. However, ES module static imports are evaluated before the importing module body runs. backfill-explore-sparklines.ts statically imports precomputeExploreSparklinesForCoins, which imports coinPriceSparkline.ts, which imports tokenPoolHistorySeries.ts. tokenPoolHistorySeries.ts captures THEGRAPH_API_KEY/GRAPH_API_KEY in a top-level const during that import chain. The script only calls loadEnvFile() later inside main(), so if the operator follows the documented usage and relies on frontend/.env rather than exporting THEGRAPH_API_KEY in the parent shell, hasGraph becomes true after loadEnvFile(), but fetchTokenPoolDayCloseSeries() still sees the earlier empty top-level THEGRAPH_API_KEY and returns null. This makes the subgraph-first backfill path silently ineffective and can cause all batches to refresh zero rows unless a Zora key is also available.

title: Canonical CSW owner checks gain unintended RPC fallback
description: Before this commit, `canonicalCswDelegation.getBaseRpcUrls()` used only `BASE_RPC_URL` entries plus `https://mainnet.base.org`, while filtering the blocked `base.llamarpc.com` host. After the change, it calls `resolveServerBaseRpcUrls()`, which always appends all global defaults, including `https://base-mainnet.public.blastapi.io`. As a result, when `BASE_RPC_URL` is `https://base.llamarpc.com,https://mainnet.base.org`, the function now returns `['https://mainnet.base.org', 'https://base-mainnet.public.blastapi.io']`, while the existing test expects only `['https://mainnet.base.org']`. This is a low-severity correctness/regression issue: owner-confirmation behavior now depends on an additional public RPC endpoint that this module did not previously include.

title: Unset backfill env vars ignore documented defaults
description: The helper readIntEnv calls Number(process.env[name] ?? '').
