In JavaScript, Number('') is 0, so when an env var is unset the function treats it as a valid value and clamps it to the configured minimum instead of returning the fallback. With the documented command that only requires DATABASE_URL and ETHOS_API_KEY, the script defaults become chainId=1 instead of 8453, totalLimit=1 instead of 10000, batchSize=50 instead of 500, maxBatches=1 instead of 100, sleepMs=0 instead of 300, and projectionLimit=100 instead of 50000. This can make the catch-up backfill process the wrong chain or almost no creators and refresh only a tiny projection slice.

title: Coinbase Wallet in-app is misclassified as Base App
description: The commit adds special handling for `Failed to fetch RPC request` / `internal error was received` failures. In `mapRemoveOwnerSubmissionError`, self-auth sessions use `isBaseAppInAppContext()` to decide whether to show Base App-only guidance or Coinbase Wallet external-browser guidance. However, `isBaseAppInAppContext()` is intentionally broad and returns true for Coinbase-branded user agents, Coinbase in-app signals, and Coinbase-injected providers. As a result, real Coinbase Wallet in-app contexts can take the Base App branch and be instructed to stay inside Base App, while the intended Chrome/Safari escape branch becomes unreachable for those environments. The new waitlist error mapping has the same risk because `WaitlistConnectBaseApp` passes the same broad detector result into `mapSubAccountOwnerInstallError`. This is a functional availability/UX regression rather than a direct security vulnerability: it can trap users in a failed signing path, but it does not bypass authentication or move funds.

title: MediaQueryList listener can break immersive scroll story
description: The new responsive scroll-story code registers a media-query change listener with mobileMq.addEventListener('change', ...). MediaQueryList.addEventListener is not available in older Safari/iOS versions that still use MediaQueryList.addListener. Because this call happens before update(), an unsupported browser raises a TypeError and aborts this inline script before it adds any is-story-* classes. The CSS hides .mkt-step elements by default and only reveals them when those classes are present, so affected browsers can see a blank/broken 'How it works' section. This is not a security vulnerability, but it is an introduced availability/UX crash on a public marketing surface. A compatible fix would feature-detect addEventListener, fall back to addListener, and ensure update() is called even if change-listener registration fails.

title: Stale CSW owner refresh can overwrite current owner state
description: The prior effect-local owner fetch used a cancelled flag during cleanup, so responses from obsolete requests were ignored. The new refreshCswOwners callback issues the same /api/deploy/smartWalletOwners request but unconditionally calls setCswOwnersState when it resolves. If canonicalCswAddress changes while a request is in flight, an older response can overwrite the current wallet's owner list. AddOwnerSigningPanel then derives installedAsOwner and canRunAddOwnerFlow from cswOwnersState.owners, so the UI can show the add-owner flow as complete or available/unavailable based on owners from a different CSW. This appears to be a client-side state consistency bug rather than an authorization bypass, because the server-side preview/execution paths still validate the authenticated user's canonical wallet and on-chain owner state.

title: Stale sub-account owner check can mark setup complete
description: The newly added `useEmbeddedOwnerOnSubAccount` hook stores only a bare `status` value and does not tie that status to the specific `(subAccountAddress, embeddedEoaAddress)` pair that was checked. When inputs change while `canCheck` is still true, `resolvedStatus` immediately returns the previous status until the asynchronous effect updates it. Consumers added in this commit use `isOwner` from that hook to decide whether waitlist setup/signing is complete. As a result, after switching accounts or sub-account addresses in the same mounted UI, a stale prior `owner` result can transiently render the new account as setup-complete/signing-ready before the new RPC check finishes. This appears to be a UI/state correctness issue rather than a direct security vulnerability, because it does not change server-side authorization or on-chain permissions.

title: Desktop chat menu clicks now minimize the chat
description: The commit changed the desktop chat header wrapper from a div to a button with onClick={onMinimize}, while also replacing the header menu's onClick stopPropagation handler with only onMouseDown and onKeyDown handlers. HeaderMenuItem buttons do not stop click propagation themselves. As a result, on desktop, clicking items in the open header menu can execute the item action and then bubble a click to the outer header button, unexpectedly minimizing the chat. This is not a security issue, but it is an introduced functional/accessibility regression and also creates invalid nested interactive controls.

title: Frontend test placement guard fails on new chart test
description: The newly added smoke test is located at frontend/src/components/explore/MetricChartPlot.test.tsx. The existing check-test-file-placement.mjs guard treats any newly added *.test.tsx file outside src/features/**, src/pages/**, or api/__tests__/** as a violation. The GitHub test workflow runs this guard via pnpm --dir frontend guard:test-file-placement. Running the guard against this commit's parent reproduces the failure: it reports src/components/explore/MetricChartPlot.test.tsx as outside the allowed locations. This is not a runtime or security vulnerability, but it is an introduced CI/release-blocking bug.

title: Enrichment failures are reported as successful refreshes
description: After the scan phase succeeds, errors from `enrichProfileWallets()` or `reconcileZoraProfilesCswIndexFlag()` are caught, checkpointed as `phase: 'enrich_failed'`, but the function still returns `{ ok: true, tick: 'refreshed' }` without surfacing the error to the API caller. The cron handler only logs warnings when `result.ok` is false, so these failures are logged as normal successful refreshes. This can hide stale wallet metadata or stale `is_in_csw_index` data from monitoring/ops. I did not find evidence that this directly enables unauthorized access, fund loss, or data exfiltration.

title: AMOE daily credits reduced below entry cost
description: AMOE entries require 100 credits, and the public API spec still describes the Twitter check-in as awarding 100 credits/day. This commit changes both AMOE_DAILY_TWITTER_CREDIT and AMOE_DAILY_XMTP_CREDIT to 1. Those constants are used directly when inserting AMOE daily point rows and in the response's awardedCredits value, so a successful daily AMOE action now grants only 1/100th of the credits needed for a minimum entry. Because AMOE is the no-purchase/free-entry path for the lottery, this undermines lottery eligibility/accounting integrity and can effectively deny users the advertised daily AMOE entry unless they accumulate many days of check-ins or other eligible points.

title: Ethos filter is applied after paginated creator fetches
description: For volume, market-cap, trending/price-change, and new creator sorts, selecting an Ethos threshold now sends ethosMin to /api/zora/explore. The handler fetches one paginated page from the Zora SDK using count/after, enriches those rows, and only then filters data.edges by ethosScore. This means the filter is page-local rather than list-global: qualifying creators that appear after low-score creators in the upstream sort are not pulled forward to fill the requested page. The API can return short or empty pages while matching creators exist later, and pageInfo/count can still describe the unfiltered upstream page. The ETHOS_SCORE path applies the threshold in SQL before OFFSET/LIMIT, but the newly enabled non-Ethos path does not.

title: Unchecked ERC4626 math lets huge-share mint drain vault
description: The Tamago ERC4626 reference implementation computes previewMint/mint, maxWithdraw, previewWithdraw, redeem, and related conversions with raw `mul`/`add` on Uint256 values instead of full-precision mulDiv or explicit overflow checks. In EVM semantics these operations wrap. For a vault with A=S=1 ether, an attacker can request roughly floor((2^256-1)/(A+1))+1 shares. The multiplication `shares * (currentAssets + 1)` wraps, so `mint` charges about 1 wei while crediting an enormous share balance. The attacker can then transfer a carefully chosen share amount to another address so `maxWithdraw` does not overflow for that address and returns about the whole honest deposit, and `withdraw` transfers those assets. This affects the newly added Tamago vault module if deployed; the existing production CreatorOVault wiring does not appear to import this module.

title: Three.js vendor rename breaks /story page
description: The `/story/` page has `<base href="/immersive/">`, so its relative import map entry resolves under `/immersive/vendor/three/...`. After this commit, the only vendored Three.js build directory is `frontend/public/immersive/vendor/three/build/`, while `/story/` still maps the bare specifier `three` to `./vendor/three/build-20260509/three.module.js`. The page then loads `/immersive/app.js`, which imports `three`; browsers will try to fetch the removed `/immersive/vendor/three/build-20260509/three.module.js`, causing module resolution failure and breaking the cinematic `/story/` experience. This is an availability/UX regression on a public static page, not a security vulnerability.

title: Recovery decoder crashes due to missing viem dependency
description: The commit adds scripts/recovery/decode-userop-signature.mjs and documents running it directly with `node decode-userop-signature.mjs <signature_hex>`. The script imports `decodeAbiParameters` from `viem`, but `viem` is not declared in the root package.json dependencies or devDependencies. Because the script lives under the repository root's scripts directory, Node's module resolution will look upward to the root node_modules, not to frontend/node_modules where viem is declared. In a clean checkout without an undeclared/hoisted phantom dependency, running the documented command fails before decoding anything with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

title: EOA-owner lane rejects standard personal_sign signatures
description: The commit introduces _submitOwnerViaPreparedCallsWithEoaOwner as an operational recovery path for on-chain EOA owners. However, it calls the signer connector with personal_sign over the userOpHash, then immediately verifies the returned signature with recoverAddress({ hash: userOpHash, signature }). Standards-compliant personal_sign implementations sign the EIP-191-prefixed digest, not the raw hash, so raw recovery will not return the EOA owner. The function therefore throws a substituted-key error for legitimate wallets such as MetaMask/Rabby/WalletConnect. This is inconsistent with the preflight guard added in the same commit, which correctly accepts both raw and EIP-191 recovery for personal_sign signatures. The likely impact is that the new EOA-owner recovery lane is unusable for many normal EOA wallets, causing an availability/operational failure rather than a direct fund-loss vulnerability.

title: Skip-vanity mode does not force zero salts
description: The commit adds a skip-vanity mode intended to force generic zero-byte CREATE2 salts for the deterministic phased deployment. However, DeployBaseMainnetDeployer._saltFromEnvOrEpoch uses bytes32(0) as the sentinel for an absent raw salt. As a result, every all-zero salt exported by deploy-base-full-release.sh is ignored. The deployment then falls back to INFRA_*_SALT_TAG values, and deploy-infra-v2.sh preserves any pre-existing INFRA_*_SALT_TAG variables instead of clearing them. This means BASE_FULL_RELEASE_SKIP_VANITY=1 does not actually force the documented zero salts and may produce unexpected deterministic addresses if stale salt-tag environment variables are present. I did not find a direct externally exploitable security issue in the commit, but this is an introduced deployment correctness bug that can undermine release reproducibility.

title: Hermit setup falsely reports failed preference saves as successful
description: The commit adds local Hermit setup commands that tell users whether their language or tone preference was persisted. However, the injected persistPreference closure in execute.ts calls upsertUserPreference and ignores its boolean success value. upsertUserPreference returns false when persistence is disabled, the DB is unavailable, validation fails, or the query errors. Because the closure catches errors and returns void, handleHermitSetupSubcommand sets saved = true after awaiting the callback, even if the underlying write did not happen. As a result, /hermit lang and /hermit tone can reply that a preference was saved when it was not, causing future Hermit replies not to honor the user’s setting and contradicting the intended storage-unavailable fallback copy.

title: AMOE rollout docs use wrong refund TTL flag
description: The new AMOE production rollout plan says abandoned burn-credit intents are refunded after `AMOE_BURN_REFUND_AGE_SEC`, defaulting to 900 seconds, and expects a refund during a 6-hour Phase 2 soak. The actual refund implementation does not read `AMOE_BURN_REFUND_AGE_SEC`; it reads `AMOE_REFUND_AGE_EPOCHS` and defaults to 7 epochs, i.e. 7 days. If operators follow this plan, they may enable `AMOE_BURN_CREDITS_ENABLED` believing the safety-net refund cron will clear abandoned burns within about 15 minutes, while the deployed code will leave those credits locked for up to a week unless the correct variable is configured.

title: Rotated Privy tokens can be silently left stale
description: The previous writer aborted before storing the identity token if either access-token or refresh-token persistence failed, preserving a consistent token set. The new code skips unchanged values, which is reasonable, but it also merely logs failures when a changed access or refresh token cannot be persisted and then proceeds to store the new identity token. That creates a split-brain credential state: the bridge consumes the fresh identity token immediately, while future refreshes still read the old access/refresh token from DB or env fallback. If Privy invalidates rotated refresh credentials, the next cron refresh will fail and the bridge will start returning auth failures after the identity token expires. The same value-only skip also cannot distinguish 'unchanged and already stored in DB' from 'unchanged but only supplied by env fallback during first bootstrap', so it can fail to copy access/refresh tokens into DB despite the documented bootstrap behavior.

title: “/meme alias” commit removes legacy /hermitimg command
description: In `executeHermitCommand`, the image-generation branch now matches only `'/meme'` and no longer accepts `'/hermitimg'`. The unsupported-command error text was also updated to list only `/meme`. This is a functional regression (API/command compatibility break) rather than a security flaw: existing integrations that still send `/hermitimg` will now fail with an unsupported command error.

title: Decision panel typo causes runtime crash in simulator
description: In the newly added `renderDecisionPanel` function, `bcBuyCoin` is defined but later logic uses `bcBuyCost`, which is undefined. When `render()` calls this function (default page state satisfies the condition), JavaScript throws a `ReferenceError`, interrupting execution and preventing normal UI updates. This is a reliability/availability bug in the client-side docs simulator, not an auth or data-exposure issue.

title: DOM XSS in AlfaClub chart via unsanitized coin symbol
description: In docs/alfaclub-lp-vs-bonding-curve-chart.html the new coinSymbol value is read directly from an input field and can also be populated from a Zora API response. That value is interpolated into HTML table rows and SVG markup that are assigned with innerHTML. Because coinSymbol is not escaped or sanitized, a malicious token symbol (or user-supplied value) containing HTML can break out of the markup and execute JavaScript in the page’s origin. If this docs page is served on the same origin as the app, this creates a DOM-based XSS risk.

title: Deploy version check now blocks after runtime config updates
description: In DeployVaultBatcher, the runtime deployment version mismatch check now compares against deploymentVersionProp, which is derived once from build-time/query settings and never updated with overrides. When the server runtime deployment version changes, the batcher sets deploymentVersionOverride but the next deploy attempt still compares against the original prop, so the mismatch persists and the handler returns early every time. This creates a self-reinforcing loop where deployments cannot proceed until the page is rebuilt/reloaded, even though an override exists.

title: Rate-limit retries can skip large log ranges
description: The updated rate-limit handling in fetchMigratedCoins retries the same log range on HTTP 429 responses, but after MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES_PER_CHUNK it advances fromBlock to toBlock+1 and skips the whole chunk without ever shrinking the range. Because the default chunkDelta was increased to 100,000 blocks, persistent 429 responses (including those triggered by oversized range requests) can cause large gaps of migration events to be skipped, leading to incomplete migrated coin detection and incorrect fee/migration status in the UI.

title: Leaderboard now ignores profiles beyond first 1000 entries
description: The commit introduces a hard cap of 1000 profiles in the eligible CTEs used for totalCount, the ranked leaderboard, and the per-user lookup. Because the cap is applied before aggregation, any profile with an id beyond the first 1000 completed profiles is not counted or ranked, and the `me` query will return null even if that user should appear. This silently truncates pagination and can skew any incentives or rewards tied to the leaderboard, allowing early profiles to dominate while later users are invisible.

title: Multi-chain swap requests blocked by Base-only allowlist
description: This commit wires the user-selected chain ID into swap execution and approval/quote API payloads. However, the server-side Uniswap guards still restrict chain IDs to Base only. When a user selects Ethereum/Arbitrum/Optimism/Polygon, the frontend sends those chain IDs and the backend rejects them as unsupported, causing the swap flow to fail. This is a functional regression introduced by the change, not a security issue.

title: Cursor sandbox config drops outbound network restrictions
description: The prior sandbox configuration enforced a default-deny egress policy with a strict allowlist. The new .cursor/sandbox.json replaces that file entirely and no longer defines a networkPolicy section, which means Cursor’s sandbox will fall back to its default egress behavior (typically allow). If secrets or credentials are present during cloud agent sessions, any executed tooling or dependency scripts can now reach arbitrary hosts and exfiltrate data or access internal metadata endpoints, removing a defense-in-depth control.
